### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>moby/moby (moby/moby)</summary>

### [`v29.4.3`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.4.3): v29.4.3

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.4.2...docker-v29.4.3)

##### 29.4.3

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.4.3 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.4.3)
- [moby/moby, 29.4.3 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.4.3)

##### Bug fixes

- **CVE-2026-31431**: Fix the 29.4.2 regression that broke 32-bit programs and i386 images. The broad socketcall(2) seccomp deny is replaced with targeted AppArmor (deny network alg) and SELinux (alg\_socket) rules that block AF\_ALG at the LSM layer, covering both socket(2) and socketcall(2) paths without disrupting legitimate 32-bit workloads. [moby/moby#52537](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52537)

  On SELinux-based systems, the SELinux mitigation requires the daemon to be configured with `selinux-enabled: true` (via `daemon.json` or the `--selinux-enabled` CLI flag). This option is not enabled by default.

- Fix the default AppArmor profile not being updated on daemon restart, requiring a system reboot to pick up profile changes from daemon upgrades. [moby/moby#52537](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52537)

</details>

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [moby/moby](https://github.com/moby/moby) | minor | `29.4.3` → `29.5.3` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>moby/moby (moby/moby)</summary>

### [`v29.5.3`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.5.3): v29.5.3

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.5.2...docker-v29.5.3)

##### 29.5.3

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.5.3 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.3)
- [moby/moby, 29.5.3 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.3)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Reduce `docker system df` errors when images are pruned at the same time with the containerd image store. [moby/moby#52672](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52672)

##### Packaging updates

- Update containerd (static binaries only) to [v2.2.4](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.4). [moby/moby#52683](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52683)
- Update Go runtime to [1.26.4](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.26.4). [moby/moby#52753](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52753), [docker/cli#7025](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7025)
- Update RootlessKit to [v3.0.1](https://github.com/rootless-containers/rootlesskit/releases/tag/v3.0.1). [moby/moby#52710](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52710)

##### Rootless

- Fix AWS IMDS access with `gvisor-tap-vsock` and UDP port forwarding for non-loopback clients. [moby/moby#52710](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52710)
- Fix installation of plugins that require host networking. [moby/moby#52735](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52735)

### [`v29.5.2`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.5.2): v29.5.2

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.5.1...docker-v29.5.2)

##### 29.5.2

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.5.2 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.2)
- [moby/moby, 29.5.2 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.2)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Fix `docker cp` failing with "mkdirat: file exists" when a container has a bind mount whose target traverses an in-container symlink (e.g. `/var/run -> /run`). [moby/moby#52655](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52655)

### [`v29.5.1`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.5.1): v29.5.1

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.5.0...docker-v29.5.1)

##### 29.5.1

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.5.1 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.1)
- [moby/moby, 29.5.1 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.1)

##### Security

This release includes fixes for multiple security vulnerabilities affecting Docker Engine.

- **CVE-2026-41567** Fix a vulnerability in `docker cp` where archive decompression binaries (e.g. `xz`, `unpigz`) were resolved via `PATH` inside the container filesystem while running as host root, allowing a malicious container to execute arbitrary binaries with host root privileges.\
  [GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r)

- **CVE-2026-41568** Fix a TOCTOU vulnerability in `docker cp` that allowed a container process to create files or directories at arbitrary locations on the host filesystem.\
  [GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5)

- **CVE-2026-42306** Fix a TOCTOU vulnerability in `docker cp` that allowed a container process to redirect a bind mount to an arbitrary location on the host filesystem.\
  [GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh)

##### Networking

- Fix UDP conntrack entries not being deleted when not bound to a specific IP address. [moby/moby#52640](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52640)

### [`v29.5.0`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.5.0): v29.5.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.4.3...docker-v29.5.0)

##### 29.5.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.5.0 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.5.0 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.0)

> \[!NOTE]
> Rootless: `gvisor-tap-vsock` is now the new default rootless network driver and should be preferred over `slirp4netns` which is no longer installed via Docker packaging.

##### New

- Rootless: Add new default  `gvisor-tap-vsock` network driver. [moby/moby#52319](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52319)
- Enable private time namespace for containers by default on supported kernels. [moby/moby#52326](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52326)
- The `local` logging driver now has support for custom attributes, adding support for the `label`, `label-regex`, `env`, `env-regex`, and `tag` log options. [moby/moby#52348](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52348)
- Windows: The daemon now supports listening on a Unix socket (`-H unix://...`), with optional group-based access control via `--group`. [moby/moby#52365](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52365)

##### Security

- CVE-2026-32288: Fix a denial of service where pulling a maliciously crafted image could cause the daemon to allocate unbounded memory when processing sparse tar archives. [GHSA-x4jj-h2v8-hqqv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x4jj-h2v8-hqqv). [moby/moby#52478](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52478)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- `docker ps --format` now supports a `.HealthStatus` placeholder to print container health state (`starting`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`) as a dedicated field. [docker/cli#6913](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6913)
- Add "time-namespaces" feature flag to disable time-namespaces. [moby/moby#52577](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52577)
- containerd integration: Fix auth token requests ignoring per-host TLS settings (custom CAs, insecure-registries). [moby/moby#52600](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52600)
- Daemon reload events now signify that the daemon reload has fully completed. [moby/moby#52589](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52589)
- Expose diagnostic data about userland proxy in `docker info`. [moby/moby#52321](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52321)
- Fix `docker image ls --filter reference=...` (`GET /images/json`) to also match fully qualified canonical image names (e.g. `docker.io/library/alpine`), not only the familiar short form. [moby/moby#52333](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52333)
- Fix a bug where leaving an autolock-enabled swarm could leave orphaned state, causing subsequent swarm init to fail with "Swarm is encrypted and needs to be unlocked". [moby/moby#52479](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52479)
- Fix an issue where logging errors appeared as empty strings in the daemon log instead of the message that failed to write. [moby/moby#52442](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52442)
- Fix incorrect SHARED SIZE and UNIQUE SIZE reporting in `docker system df -v` by including shared content blobs in size calculation. [moby/moby#52482](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52482)
- Fix support for CDI specifications that request additional group IDs. [moby/moby#52579](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52579)
- Fix volume subpath file mounts over an existing file in the image failing container creation with "not a directory". [moby/moby#52584](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52584)
- Sort labels in `volume`, `network`, `config`, and `secret` formatters for deterministic output. [docker/cli#6954](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6954)
- Swarm: Prevent corruption of Raft snapshots when swarm state is large. [moby/moby#52441](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52441)

##### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.30.0](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.30.0). [moby/moby#52618](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52618)
- Update Go runtime to [1.26.3](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.26.3). [moby/moby#52572](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52572), [docker/cli#6967](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6967)

##### Networking

- Fix conntrack entries being incorrectly deleted for UDP containers sharing the same port on different IPs when one container is restarted. [moby/moby#52423](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52423)
- Fix stale VIP DNS records for swarm service network aliases not being removed during rolling updates. [moby/moby#52236](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52236)
- Fix the userland proxy silently dropping UDP datagrams when a previous write to an unavailable backend left a stale ECONNREFUSED error on the socket. [moby/moby#52483](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52483)
- Rootless: Properly support `--net=host` and localhost registries. [moby/moby#47103](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/47103)

##### Rootless

- Update RootlessKit to [v3.0.0](https://github.com/rootless-containers/rootlesskit/releases/tag/v3.0.0). [moby/moby#52319](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52319)

##### Go SDK

- cli/config/configfile: `GetAuthConfig`, `GetCredentialsStore`: normalize hostname when resolving auth. [docker/cli#6846](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6846)

##### Deprecations

- cli/command/image/build: remove deprecated `DefaultDockerfileName` const. [docker/cli#6737](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6737)
- cli/command/image/build: remove deprecated `DetectArchiveReader` util. [docker/cli#6737](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6737)
- cli/command/image/build: remove deprecated `IsArchive` utility. [docker/cli#6737](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6737)
- cli/command/image/build: remove deprecated `ResolveAndValidateContextPath` util. [docker/cli#6737](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6737)
- cli/command/image/build: remove deprecated `WriteTempDockerfile` util. [docker/cli#6737](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6737)

</details>

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>moby/moby (moby/moby)</summary>

### [`v29.6.1`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.6.1): v29.6.1

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.6.0-rc.1...docker-v29.6.1)

##### 29.6.1

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.6.1 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.6.1)
- [moby/moby, 29.6.1 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.6.1)

##### Security

This release includes fixes for multiple security vulnerabilities affecting Docker Engine.

- A malicious image could supply a malicious `/etc/passwd` or `/etc/group`-style file causing excessive memory consumption, potentially resulting in process termination due to Out Of Memory (OOM) conditions. [GHSA-mjcv-p78q-w5fw](https://github.com/moby/sys/security/advisories/GHSA-mjcv-p78q-w5fw), [GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-jpcc-p29g-p8mq), [GHSA-72x6-4j93-7w86](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-72x6-4j93-7w86)
- A custom frontend could send a crafted build request that disabled Seccomp and AppArmor protections for the build container, even if the user did not explicitly allow the security.insecure entitlement. Other security measures, like Linux capabilities were still applied to these containers. [GHSA-7236-3392-c5c6](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-7236-3392-c5c6)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Update containerd (static binaries) to [v2.2.5](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.5). [moby/moby#52950](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52950)

##### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.31.1](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.31.1). [moby/moby#52954](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52954)

### [`v29.6.0`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.6.0): v29.6.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.5.3...docker-v29.6.0-rc.1)

##### 29.6.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.6.0 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.6.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.6.0 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.6.0)

##### New

- `POST /containers/{id}/update` now supports per-device blkio resource settings. [moby/moby#52651](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52651)
- Add `GET /images/{name}/attestations` endpoint to retrieve in-toto attestation statements (such as SLSA provenance and SPDX SBOM) attached to an image. Supports optional platform selection, predicate type filtering, and a statement query parameter for verbatim statement bodies.

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- `docker image push` now respects `NO_COLOR`. [docker/cli#6957](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6957)
- containerd image store: Fix `docker system prune` to include unpacked image data when reporting reclaimed space. [moby/moby#52905](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52905)
- Fix `docker system df` image size reporting to count only snapshots directly used by images. [moby/moby#52901](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52901)
- Fix a bug where registry authentication failures during worker image pulls were reported as a misleading “No such image” error. [moby/moby#52698](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52698)
- Fix default BuildKit GC policy to prune reproducible cache types as intended. [moby/moby#52814](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52814)
- Fix explicit file modes being filtered by the daemon umask, including `COPY --chmod` permissions. [moby/moby#52892](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52892)
- Fix image selection with the containerd image store on amd64 hosts when images provide amd64 variant-specific manifests. [moby/moby#52773](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52773)
- The `--password` flag on `docker login` now accepts `-` to pass the password through STDIN as alternative to `--password-stdin`. [docker/cli#7029](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7029)

##### Packaging updates

- Update runc (in static binaries) to [v1.3.6](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/tag/v1.3.6). [moby/moby#52883](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52883)
- Update BuildKit to [v0.31.0](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.31.0). [moby/moby#52904](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52904)

##### Networking

- Allow the nftables firewall mode to be used with a daemon that is linked against libnftables when the `nft` command is not installed on the system. [moby/moby#52820](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52820)
- Don't publish container ports on host ports listed in `net.ipv4.ip_local_reserved_ports` when dynamically allocating ports. [moby/moby#52818](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52818)
- Fix a race condition in overlay network bulk sync that caused \~30s DNS resolution delays on newly joined swarm nodes. [moby/moby#52862](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52862)
- Mitigate a crash in libnftables when using nftables as the firewall backend by changing the default build option to execute the `nft` command instead. Users building dockerd from source can opt into linking against libnftables by building with the `libnftables` build tag. [moby/moby#52886](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52886)

##### Rootless

- Silence the spurious warning "IPv4 forwarding is disabled". [moby/moby#52742](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52742)

##### Deprecations

- The Engine now returns a deprecation warning when a container connected to the default bridge is created with links specified. [moby/moby#47427](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/47427)

### [`v29.5.3`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.5.3): v29.5.3

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.5.2...docker-v29.5.3)

##### 29.5.3

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.5.3 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.3)
- [moby/moby, 29.5.3 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.3)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Reduce `docker system df` errors when images are pruned at the same time with the containerd image store. [moby/moby#52672](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52672)

##### Packaging updates

- Update containerd (static binaries only) to [v2.2.4](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.2.4). [moby/moby#52683](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52683)
- Update Go runtime to [1.26.4](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.26.4). [moby/moby#52753](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52753), [docker/cli#7025](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7025)
- Update RootlessKit to [v3.0.1](https://github.com/rootless-containers/rootlesskit/releases/tag/v3.0.1). [moby/moby#52710](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52710)

##### Rootless

- Fix AWS IMDS access with `gvisor-tap-vsock` and UDP port forwarding for non-loopback clients. [moby/moby#52710](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52710)
- Fix installation of plugins that require host networking. [moby/moby#52735](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52735)

### [`v29.5.2`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.5.2): v29.5.2

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.5.1...docker-v29.5.2)

##### 29.5.2

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.5.2 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.2)
- [moby/moby, 29.5.2 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.2)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Fix `docker cp` failing with "mkdirat: file exists" when a container has a bind mount whose target traverses an in-container symlink (e.g. `/var/run -> /run`). [moby/moby#52655](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52655)

### [`v29.5.1`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.5.1): v29.5.1

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.5.0...docker-v29.5.1)

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.5.1 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.1)
- [moby/moby, 29.5.1 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.1)

##### Security

This release includes fixes for multiple security vulnerabilities affecting Docker Engine.

- **CVE-2026-41567** Fix a vulnerability in `docker cp` where archive decompression binaries (e.g. `xz`, `unpigz`) were resolved via `PATH` inside the container filesystem while running as host root, allowing a malicious container to execute arbitrary binaries with host root privileges.\
  [GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r)

- **CVE-2026-41568** Fix a TOCTOU vulnerability in `docker cp` that allowed a container process to create files or directories at arbitrary locations on the host filesystem.\
  [GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5)

- **CVE-2026-42306** Fix a TOCTOU vulnerability in `docker cp` that allowed a container process to redirect a bind mount to an arbitrary location on the host filesystem.\
  [GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh)

##### Networking

- Fix UDP conntrack entries not being deleted when not bound to a specific IP address. [moby/moby#52640](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52640)

### [`v29.5.0`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.5.0): v29.5.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.4.3...docker-v29.5.0)

##### 29.5.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.5.0 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.5.0 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.5.0)

> \[!NOTE]
> Rootless: `gvisor-tap-vsock` is now the new default rootless network driver and should be preferred over `slirp4netns` which is no longer installed via Docker packaging.

##### New

- Rootless: Add new default  `gvisor-tap-vsock` network driver. [moby/moby#52319](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52319)
- Enable private time namespace for containers by default on supported kernels. [moby/moby#52326](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52326)
- The `local` logging driver now has support for custom attributes, adding support for the `label`, `label-regex`, `env`, `env-regex`, and `tag` log options. [moby/moby#52348](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52348)
- Windows: The daemon now supports listening on a Unix socket (`-H unix://...`), with optional group-based access control via `--group`. [moby/moby#52365](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52365)

##### Security

- CVE-2026-32288: Fix a denial of service where pulling a maliciously crafted image could cause the daemon to allocate unbounded memory when processing sparse tar archives. [GHSA-x4jj-h2v8-hqqv](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-x4jj-h2v8-hqqv). [moby/moby#52478](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52478)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- `docker ps --format` now supports a `.HealthStatus` placeholder to print container health state (`starting`, `healthy`, `unhealthy`) as a dedicated field. [docker/cli#6913](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6913)
- Add "time-namespaces" feature flag to disable time-namespaces. [moby/moby#52577](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52577)
- containerd integration: Fix auth token requests ignoring per-host TLS settings (custom CAs, insecure-registries). [moby/moby#52600](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52600)
- Daemon reload events now signify that the daemon reload has fully completed. [moby/moby#52589](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52589)
- Expose diagnostic data about userland proxy in `docker info`. [moby/moby#52321](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52321)
- Fix `docker image ls --filter reference=...` (`GET /images/json`) to also match fully qualified canonical image names (e.g. `docker.io/library/alpine`), not only the familiar short form. [moby/moby#52333](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52333)
- Fix a bug where leaving an autolock-enabled swarm could leave orphaned state, causing subsequent swarm init to fail with "Swarm is encrypted and needs to be unlocked". [moby/moby#52479](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52479)
- Fix an issue where logging errors appeared as empty strings in the daemon log instead of the message that failed to write. [moby/moby#52442](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52442)
- Fix incorrect SHARED SIZE and UNIQUE SIZE reporting in `docker system df -v` by including shared content blobs in size calculation. [moby/moby#52482](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52482)
- Fix support for CDI specifications that request additional group IDs. [moby/moby#52579](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52579)
- Fix volume subpath file mounts over an existing file in the image failing container creation with "not a directory". [moby/moby#52584](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52584)
- Sort labels in `volume`, `network`, `config`, and `secret` formatters for deterministic output. [docker/cli#6954](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6954)
- Swarm: Prevent corruption of Raft snapshots when swarm state is large. [moby/moby#52441](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52441)

body:
Phase 1 of the config/overhaul work: retire the per-storage-type duplication behind the two do-spaces field incidents.

## What
Two shared helpers in `lib/core/config-loader.sh`, used by all three call sites (`duplicacy_primary_backup`, `duplicacy_add_backup`, `duplicacy_init_for_restore`):

- `build_storage_url <id>` — pure: the `local`/`sftp`/`b2`/`s3` URL string, one definition.
- `export_duplicacy_storage_secrets <id>` — the `sanitize -> UPPER -> DUPLICACY_<NAME>_*` credential-env mapping, one definition (the surface that broke in 0.8.10 and 0.8.11).

Once the URL is a variable, the `init`/`add` command is identical across types, so each function's 4-way branch collapses to one init/add call plus a small per-type block for the leftover `duplicacy set` credential writes. Net -92 lines behind the diffstat; 3 copies -> 1 for both concerns.

## No behavior change
- 11 new bats tests (`tests/storage_target.bats`) pin `build_storage_url` (all four types, region default, unsupported, target-specific id) and `export_duplicacy_storage_secrets` (per-type vars + the `do-spaces -> DUPLICACY_DO_SPACES_*` incident lock).
- Full suite 23/23 green; shellcheck clean (no new warnings); image builds; the `local` backup->restore roundtrip passes with content + mode + UID/GID preserved.

## Coverage note
The roundtrip only exercises `local` end-to-end (no creds/network in CI). `sftp`/`b2`/`s3` rest on the bats string-level tests + line-by-line preservation — which is the reason for collapsing them to a single definition each.

body:
Phase 2 of the overhaul: replace the in-container Debian `cron` daemon with [supercronic](https://github.com/aptible/supercronic) and drop the `SETGID` capability.

## Why
`cron` forks with `setgid` to exec jobs, which is why the hardened `cap_drop: ALL` template had to add `SETGID` back. supercronic runs jobs as the container user, so `SETGID` is no longer needed and is removed from the documented cap set (now `DAC_OVERRIDE` + `CHOWN` + `FOWNER`). supercronic also passes the container environment straight through (Debian cron scrubs it), which unblocks the later env-native-config phase.

## What
- **Dockerfile**: drop `cron`, add `tzdata`, download supercronic (Renovate-pinned via `# renovate:` comment, tracked by the existing `dockerfileVersions` preset).
- **docker-entrypoint.sh**: cron block → `supercronic -test` (fail-fast on a bad `CRON_SCHEDULE`) + backgrounded `supercronic -passthrough-logs & wait` — **not** `exec`, so the SIGTERM graceful-stop trap and log-tailer still work.
- **Caps**: `SETGID` removed from `compose.yaml`, `README.md` (both cap blocks + table + note + daemon-mode line), the round-trip doc comment, and the CI integration invocation.
- **New test** `tests/integration/scheduler.sh` + a step in the `integration` CI job: fires a scheduled job under `cap_drop: ALL` with **no `SETGID`** and asserts it ran.

## Interface unchanged
`CRON_SCHEDULE` (standard 5-field) and `TZ` behave exactly as before — old compose files with `SETGID` still run fine (the cap just becomes unused). Only edge: supercronic rejects `@reboot`/`@midnight`/`@every` (never documented), and the new `-test` makes an unsupported schedule fail loudly at startup instead of silently never firing.

## Validation (local, amd64)
Image builds (supercronic present, cron absent); round-trip passes **without SETGID** (content + mode + UID/GID preserved); scheduler smoke passes **without SETGID**; shellcheck clean; bats 23/23.

Version bump is intentionally **not** in this PR — `release.yml` (dispatch `bump=patch` → 0.8.12) owns the CHANGELOG promotion and image-tag bump.

ENV SUPERCRONIC_URL=https://github.com/aptible/supercronic/releases/download/v0.2.47/supercronic-linux-amd64 \

 && echo "${SUPERCRONIC_SHA1SUM}  ${SUPERCRONIC}" | sha1sum -c - \

body:
Env-native configuration as a dual-mode alternative to the encrypted bundle. Config resolves in three layers of increasing precedence: the bundle's `config.sh` (optional baseline / cold-restore path), plain env vars for non-secret settings, and files for secrets (`<NAME>_FILE` or `/run/secrets/<name>`; a secret passed as a raw env var is purged). RSA/SSH keys are materialized from mounted files. This lets a deployment migrate off the bundle one value at a time, or run fully env-native (a k8s ConfigMap + Secret) with no bundle at all.

Also in this change:
- `SERVICE_DIRECTORIES` accepts a colon/newline-delimited scalar (fits one env var or a YAML block); the legacy bash-array form is still read.
- `config-loader` fails fast when `STORAGE_PASSWORD` is shorter than 8 characters (a Duplicacy storage-init requirement) instead of surfacing later as an opaque failure.
- Stale "edit config.sh" guidance in error messages reworded to be mode-neutral.

No version bump (the release workflow owns that). Verified locally: bats 36/36, shellcheck clean, changelog lint OK, plus a bundle-mode round-trip regression, an env-native round-trip, and a successful env-native backup through the real entrypoint (snapshots written) - all under `cap_drop: ALL`.

body:
**BREAKING:** `BUNDLE_PASSWORD` is no longer read from the environment. It is now a file-based secret: read from `BUNDLE_PASSWORD_FILE` if set, otherwise `/run/secrets/bundle_password`. A container that still sets `BUNDLE_PASSWORD` in its environment fails fast at startup with a migration message, rather than silently dropping into env-native mode and failing later with a confusing "no bundle" error.

Rationale: the bundle password decrypts the entire bundle (including the RSA private key), so holding it in an env var leaked it via `docker inspect` and `/proc`. This completes the file-only secrets model from the env-native change.

Docker secrets: `/run/secrets/<name>` is the native Docker/k8s secret mount path, so a Compose or Swarm `secrets:` entry named `bundle_password` is picked up automatically (same `<NAME>_FILE` + `/run/secrets` idiom as the official postgres/mysql images). The compose template and README examples now use `secrets:`.

Migration: write the password to a file, mount it at `/run/secrets/bundle_password`, and remove `BUNDLE_PASSWORD` from `environment:` / `env_file`.

Verified locally: fail-fast on an env `BUNDLE_PASSWORD`; a bundle decrypts from a mounted password file through the real entrypoint and backs up (Docker-secret style); env-native round-trip regression passes. New `tests/integration/bundle-secret.sh` guards the DR path; the CI smoke also asserts the env fail-fast.

No version bump (the release workflow owns that); accumulates under `[Unreleased]` toward the single `0.9.0`.

body:
Completes the env-native rework's two-way street.

- **`archiver migrate [OUTPUT_DIR]`** (new) reads the *effective* config and writes env-native adoption materials: `archiver.env` (non-secret `KEY=value`, for a Compose `environment:` block or a k8s ConfigMap) and a `secrets/` dir with one file per secret plus the RSA/SSH keys (Docker secrets / k8s Secret / openbao). The bundle is left untouched.
- **`bundle export` is now mode-agnostic**: it serializes the effective (env-merged) config into the bundle, so a fully env-native deployment can regenerate a portable encrypted bundle for cold restore / DR.
- **`bundle import`**: the SSH keypair is now optional (only sftp needs it); the RSA keypair is what is required. This lets a bundle exported from an env-native deployment (which may have no SSH key) re-import cleanly.

Under the hood: the config var surface (non-secret vs secret regexes) is factored into `config-loader.sh` as a single source of truth, reused by the loader and by the new `config-serialize.sh`, so a serializer can never silently drop a field the loader knows about.

Verified locally: full round-trip `bundle -> migrate -> env-native backup -> mode-agnostic export -> re-import` passes; migrate emits secret-free env + complete secret/key files; all existing integration tests (round-trip, env-native, bundle-secret, scheduler) and bats 36/36 still pass. New `tests/integration/migrate.sh` runs the whole round-trip in CI.

No version bump; accumulates under `[Unreleased]` toward the single `0.9.0`.

title: feat: add 'archiver migrate' + mode-agnostic 'bundle export'

body:
Phase 4: least-privilege backup/restore capability profiles.

`CHOWN` and `FOWNER` are only used by restore (to recreate original UID/GID and set modes on other-UID files). So a backup-only deployment can run with just `DAC_OVERRIDE` and add `CHOWN` + `FOWNER` only when restoring.

To keep that safe (a bare cap split would quietly reintroduce the old silent-root-ownership bug), restore now **warns without ever blocking**: if it would preserve ownership but the container lacks `CHOWN`/`FOWNER`, it logs a clear warning that files will land root-owned and how to fix it. The restore always proceeds (the data is what matters in DR); set `IGNORE_OWNERSHIP=1` to restore without ownership on purpose. The capability check reads `/proc/self/status` `CapEff` (no side effects, no false positives) and short-circuits when `-ignore-owner` is in effect.

Docs: README cap table + a "backup-only least privilege" note + both cap_add examples updated; compose.yaml notes CHOWN/FOWNER are restore-only and droppable.

Verified locally: warns under backup-only caps, silent under full caps, silent with -ignore-owner; the normal restore round-trip is unaffected (no spurious warning); bats 36/36. New `tests/integration/restore-caps.sh` runs under both cap sets in CI.

No version bump; final piece of the env-native rework, accumulating under `[Unreleased]` toward `0.9.0`.

body:
Fixes the two archiver findings from the 2026-07-04 fleet audit, both verified live before fixing.

**Critical: a failed primary backup reported success.** `$!` after the backgrounded `duplicacy | log_output &` pipeline is the log reader (last pipeline element), which exits 0 regardless of duplicacy. A failed backup logged "completed", notified success, and exited 0 (regression from the graceful-stop commit; pre-stop code checked `PIPESTATUS[0]`). Fixed with process substitution (`> >(log_output) 2>&1 &`): `$!` is duplicacy itself, `wait` returns its real status, and duplicacy stays a **direct child** of main.sh, which pause/resume/stop (`pkill -P LOCK_PID`) depend on. A subshell+pipefail fix would have made it a grandchild and silently broken all three.

**High: `archiver stop` during the final service backup ran the destructive wrap-up anyway.** The early `return 1` bypassed the per-service stop handler, so the run continued into check + `prune -exhaustive` + secondary copies and recorded a successful completion. main() now honors the stop flag after the service loop, before wrap-up; a stop is no longer counted as an error; and an empty `last_working_dir` (all services failed) skips wrap-up instead of pruning from whatever directory was left (`cd ""` is a silent no-op in bash).

Also: graceful stop now TERMs duplicacy directly (previously it killed the log reader and waited for duplicacy to die of a broken pipe — observed blocking 15s in the repro).

New deterministic regression tests (duplicacy shadowed by a wrapper that fails/blocks only the `backup` subcommand), both wired into CI: `backup-failure.sh`, `stop-skips-prune.sh`. Both FAIL on the pre-fix image and PASS post-fix. Full suite green: 6/6 existing integration, bats 36/36, shellcheck parity, pause/resume/stop verified live under the new process tree.

title: fix: report failed primary backups and honor stop before storage wrap-up

body:
Comprehensive test build-out plus the five bugs writing it surfaced.

**New integration tests (13).** In-container: copy-path (secondary storage receives the backup, restores from it, and a failing `duplicacy copy` is reported), multi-service (glob expansion, one wrap-up, per-service failure isolation), lock-concurrency (busy refusal, stale-lock recovery), pause-resume (pause freezes duplicacy to state T, resume completes, stop-while-paused kills), stop-nonfinal (stop honored at the next service boundary), service-settings (filters shape the snapshot; hooks ordered and isolated), healthcheck (four states), restore-extras (revision pinning, IGNORE_OWNERSHIP, restore-service.sh hook). Host-driven, in a new parallel `integration-host` CI job: sigterm-stop (real `docker stop` mid-backup exits gracefully in seconds, no prune), invalid-cron (fail-fast), s3-minio (backup+restore over the s3 wire against a TLS MinIO sidecar — virtual-host addressing, exactly like Spaces/AWS), sftp-runtime (backup+restore over ssh against an sshd sidecar). The storage sidecar tests exercise the exact production `build_storage_url` + `DUPLICACY_<NAME>_*` code paths that string-level tests missed in 0.8.10/0.8.11.

**New bats (36 → 64):** lockfile.sh semantics, SERVICE_DIRECTORIES glob expansion, config-serialize round-trips (metacharacter-heavy secrets byte-exact through both output shapes), format_duration.

**Fixes the tests surfaced:**
1. `acquire_lock` stale recovery removed the dead lock but never re-took it — the recovered run was lockless (stop/status/pause blind; a concurrent backup would be admitted). It now re-acquires.
2. A backup refused because one is already running now explains itself instead of exiting 1 silently.
3. `archiver healthcheck` reported healthy env-native deployments (no config.sh) permanently UNHEALTHY, and its finished-run detection grepped a log line nothing emits ("Archiver script completed"); it now recognizes env-native mode and matches the real end-of-run marker.
4. The entrypoint SIGTERM handler exited immediately after `archiver stop`, racing PID-namespace teardown against the backup recording its stop — it now waits (bounded under the 2m grace period) for the lock to clear.
5. Env-native SFTP could back up but not restore: `ssh_public_key` was never placed by the entrypoint nor exported by `archiver migrate`, and the restore path requires both key halves. Docs updated (README, compose.yaml).

Verified locally against the built image: 16/16 in-container integration, 4/4 host-driven, 64/64 bats, entrypoint smokes. The release gate now also requires the `integration-host` job.

body:
0.9.0 transition era: env-native configuration becomes the first-class citizen, plus every blocker and should-fix finding from the 62-agent pre-release audit.

**Env-native first-class (owner direction: the bundle will ultimately be dropped; 0.9.0 is the transition era).** `archiver init` now emits ready-to-deploy env-native materials (`env-native/archiver.env` + `secrets/`, via the migrate serializer) alongside the encrypted bundle, and its guidance leads with the env-native deployment. The shipped `compose.yaml` flips to an env-native primary service with bundle mode as the commented transitional alternative; the README installation and Configuration Sources sections are reframed accordingly; CHANGELOG gains a `### Breaking` section (BUNDLE_PASSWORD file-only) that will lead the release notes and a `### Deprecated` section declaring the transition.

**Audit blockers fixed:** release.yml's own pre-tag smoke asserted a removed error string (every 0.9.0 dispatch would have aborted); init serialized the container's inherited environment/secrets and its own working variables into fresh bundles — a multi-directory init kept only the first directory, and `docker compose run ... init` folded the OLD deployment's config into a cold-restore artifact paired with a NEW RSA key (fixed via `ARCHIVER_CONFIG_IGNORE_OVERLAYS`, which actively clears env config vars — skipping the overlay was proven insufficient by the new test); the raw-env secret purge now warns per variable naming the file path to use; a mounted bundle with no resolvable password fails fast with a precise message instead of a misleading "no bundle" error or a silent env-native fall-through; `ARCHIVER_BUNDLE_PASSWORD` is unset after import (it stayed exported to every child process — the exact /proc leak the breaking change is justified by); openssl now takes the bundle password via `-pass fd:` instead of argv (same key derivation, old bundles still decrypt — test-proven); migrate/init write with umask 077; the README's DR guidance now lists exactly what to escrow (the old text implied the RSA key alone decrypts backups); the migrate example actually lands its output on the host.

**Also:** CRLF secret files handled; dangling `<NAME>_FILE` is a hard error; `archiver bundle import` self-resolves so the documented `docker exec` invocation works; interactive restore honors `IGNORE_OWNERSHIP=1`; `ENV BUNDLE_PASSWORD=""` stub removed from the image; release-gating sidecar images digest-pinned; one-off-restore/hostname-snapshot-ID/image-tags/b2-s3-secrets docs corrected; stale tool lists fixed; the orphaned `env-native.sh` test is finally wired into CI.

**New tests:** `init-envnative.sh` (scripted init with decoy deployment env + decoy secrets, multi-directory answers, bundle tar-mode 0600, legacy `-k` decrypt compat, bundle-free backup from the emitted materials), `entrypoint-secrets.sh` (three precise-error negatives + no-password-in-any-process-environ hygiene), 4 new bats (64 → 68).

Verified locally: 17/17 in-container integration, 5/5 host-driven, bats 68/68 on the CI image, both entrypoint smokes incl. the new release.yml assertions. Note: this PR touches the Dockerfile, so CI includes the arm64 qemu build.

body:
Adds the automatic recovery kit: with the recovery_password secret present, each backup serializes the full effective configuration (settings, every secret, keys), generated RECREATE.txt recreation notes, and any deployment manifests mounted at /opt/archiver/deployment (compose bind / k8s ConfigMap / NixOS bind, captured verbatim), encrypts it (AES-256 pbkdf2), and uploads it as a plain file beside the duplicacy data on every storage target. Recovery = any one storage location + the single password, decrypted with stock openssl on any machine. init generates the password and displays it once; the compose template mounts the secret and its own compose.yaml, and consumes archiver.env via env_file. Re-uploaded only on content change; per-target state with automatic retry of failed targets; failures notify but never fail the backup.

Also removes /opt/archiver/bundle from the image VOLUME declaration: Compose carries the previous container mount over for image-declared volume paths on recreate, so converting a bundle-mode deployment to env-native with --force-recreate inherited the old bundle mount and crash-looped on the bundle-without-password fail-fast (hit live during the NAS conversion).

Testing: 74 bats (incl. B2 JSON client vs realistic API responses, fingerprint runtime-mutation immunity, ConfigMap-style capture); new recovery-kit integration suite (produce/decrypt/self-contained/manifest+notes/no-rewrite/update/force/prune-exhaustive-safe/multi-target partial-failure retry/same-password refusal); sftp + s3 wire suites extended with real kit upload/retrieve/decrypt; init-envnative extended (kit on by default, decryptable with the generated password); full gate run twice back-to-back, 18/18 green. The B2 native-API upload leg has no CI double (unit-tested parser only) and gets live verification on the NAS right after release.

body: Owner-found: `archiver start` while a backup is running printed the success line and exited 0 — the refusal happens inside the backgrounded main.sh whose output is discarded. Sibling bug: `restart` raced the asynchronously-stopping backup and could stop-but-never-start, silently. Fix: the dispatcher pre-checks the lock (visible refusal, non-zero exit; stale locks still start) and restart waits up to 120s for lock release with a clear failure message if cleanup outlasts it. lockfile.sh no longer sources logging (only log_lockfile_summary needed it and its callers provide it), making it dependency-free so the dispatcher shares is_lock_valid/get_lock_pid instead of duplicating the check — sourcing the logging chain in the dispatcher mutates the environment the backgrounded child inherits (config-loader arrays SERVICE_DIRECTORIES, arrays do not export). lock-concurrency test extended: async-start refusal (exit code + message + no false success line) and restart stop-wait-start. NOT for immediate release — rides the next patch.

body:
Splits the single nightly run into two independent pipelines so storage check/prune no longer inflate every backup, and hardens the concurrency model. Intended release: 0.10.0 (minor; contains breaking changes).

## Highlights
- Backup pipeline is hooks -> backup -> parallel copies only; check + prune move to a separate `archiver maintenance` pipeline with its own schedule (`MAINTENANCE_SCHEDULE`), lock, and log (`maintenance.log`).
- Secondary copies run in parallel (overlap bandwidth-free enumeration with upload on upload-capped links); each leg reaped as it finishes.
- Per-storage locks serialize a copy against a check/prune on the same storage; the copy also holds the primary source lock for its duration. Atomic reap-by-rename + hardlink-create primitives; stop-aware waits.
- `PRUNE_EXHAUSTIVE_FREQUENCY` (off/daily/weekly/monthly, default monthly) runs the expensive `-exhaustive` GC on its own per-storage interval, with belated firing on sparse schedules.

## Breaking
- `CRON_SCHEDULE` -> `BACKUP_SCHEDULE` (container fails fast if the old name is set); new `MAINTENANCE_SCHEDULE` (unset = manual maintenance only).
- `ROTATE_BACKUPS` -> `PRUNE_BACKUPS` (old name still translated for bundle configs), plus `CHECK_BACKUPS`.
- `archiver start`/`restart` and `backup prune|retain` removed (they error with guidance). New surface: `archiver backup [--detach]`, `archiver maintenance [exhaustive]`, `archiver stop [backup|maintenance|all] [--immediate]`.

## Validation
- 87 bats, shellcheck parity, and all integration suites (including the new maintenance suite) pass locally.
- Multi-agent audit of the full release: 73 findings verified, fixes applied and re-validated.

## Rollout note
Deployments still on `CRON_SCHEDULE` fail fast on this image, so the nas/vps env rename (+ `MAINTENANCE_SCHEDULE`, + vps `drill.nix`) must ride the same PR as the image bump. Version bump is left to the release workflow.
head: refs/pull/60/head
title: feat: split backups and maintenance into independent pipelines

body:
Runs the backup and maintenance pipelines concurrently by removing the per-storage lock subsystem, relying on Duplicacy's own lock-free design instead.

Motivation: the primary-source lock held for the whole copy phase meant maintenance serialized behind an in-progress copy (on a long night, maintenance fired and then waited hours for the copy to finish). A workflow audit of the Duplicacy **v3.2.5** source (adversarial red-team, line-cited) confirmed the locking was unnecessary for data safety: a non-exclusive `check`/`prune` running alongside a `copy` on the same storage can, at worst, make the copy abort loudly — never corrupt a storage, delete referenced data, or leave a partial secondary. Two structural guarantees: a copy reads a mid-prune fossil via the `.fsl` fallback, and it writes the destination snapshot file **last** (after all chunks upload).

Changes:
- Remove the per-storage lock primitives (`lib/core/lockfile.sh`), `STORAGE_LOCK_PREFIX`, the acquire/wait/release calls in the copy phase and `maintain_storage`, both EXIT-trap lock reaps, the entrypoint boot cleanup of storage locks, and the healthcheck storage-lock reporting.
- The copy phase now retries a failed leg **once** automatically (`run_copy_legs` helper) to absorb the rare, transient contention; a fresh copy re-enumerates and resumes. Only a second failure is reported as an error.
- Net **-253 lines**.

Safety guardrail (unchanged, reconfirmed): the maintenance pipeline never emits `prune -exclusive` (the one flag that would make concurrency unsafe); `-exhaustive` is safe and does not imply it.

Validation: build, 78 bats, CI-parity shellcheck, and 10 integration suites all pass — including a new copy-path scenario asserting a leg that fails once then succeeds is retried to a clean run. No config/API/env change; ships as a patch (0.10.1).

  - remove control characters (\x00-\x08\x0B\x0C\x0E-\x1F) ([#​1176](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/issues/1176))
  - don't report (skipped) last test as failed when `teardown_suite` generates FD3 output ([#​1181](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/issues/1181))

- `run` now honors `set -e` in your functions ([#​1118](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/issues/1118))
  - **ATTENTION**: In previous versions this was suppressed unintentionally.
    While it might constitute a breaking change for some, we decided the new behavior should be the default because it might uncover hidden errors.
    If you need the old behavior, you can use this wrapper function `suppress_errexit() { "$@​" || return $?; }` like `run suppress_errexit <your command...>`
- avoid overwriting `$_` by the DEBUG and ERR traps set by Bats ([#​1208](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/issues/1208))
- fail with error when receiving empty string as testfile path ([#​1212](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/issues/1212))

- update the default version of the `bash` Docker image to 5.3 in `devcontainer` ([#​1184](https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core/issues/1184))

body:
The automatic recovery kit was placed `root:600`, so a non-root backup/mirror user pulling the datastore could not read it (rsync exits 23 on that one file). The kit is already encrypted and lives inside the datastore, so it now inherits that storage's ownership/permissions instead of being a locked-down outlier:

- **local**: stamped to match the storage's own Duplicacy `config` (owner:group + mode)
- **sftp**: inherits the connecting user's umask/ownership (same access model Duplicacy's chunks get over that connection)
- **b2/s3**: unaffected (no POSIX permissions)

Existing deployments self-correct once on the first backup (or `archiver recovery-kit`) run after upgrade: a placement-scheme version is folded into the change-detection fingerprint, forcing a one-time re-stamp even when the kit content is unchanged (no `recovery-kit force` needed).

body:
0.10.2 made the recovery kit share the datastore's access model, but only on **local** storage targets. On **SFTP** targets the kit was still placed with the connecting user's umask, so where that user's umask is restrictive (e.g. `server` with `077`) the kit landed owner-only and a separate mirror/backup user could not read it — the outlier 0.10.2 set out to remove.

The SFTP upload now reads the mode of the storage's own `config` file and applies it to the kit and its README with a best-effort `chmod` after upload (a server that forbids `SETSTAT` still yields a successful upload), matching what the local path already does. The placement-scheme version is bumped again, so existing deployments re-stamp their already-placed kit once on the first backup (or `archiver recovery-kit`) run after upgrade.

- `symbolic_mode_to_octal` + `recovery_kit_sftp_ref_mode` read `config`'s mode over sftp; unit-tested in `recovery_kit.bats`.
- `tests/integration/sftp-runtime.sh` now asserts the placed kit's mode follows the storage `config` mode.
- Verified locally: bats unit suite, the sftp-runtime integration test, and the local recovery-kit integration test all pass.
