This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [moby/moby](https://github.com/moby/moby) | minor | `29.6.2` → `29.9.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>moby/moby</summary>

### [`v29.9.0`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.9.0): v29.9.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.8.2...docker-v29.9.0-rc.2)

##### 29.9.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.9.0 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.9.0 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.0)

##### Security

The Go runtime update fixes the following security vulnerabilities in Docker Engine:

- **CVE-2026-97032**: An HTTP/2 client could crash the daemon by changing the HPACK header table size while sending requests. [golang/go#81867](https://go.dev/issue/81867)
- **CVE-2026-78659**: An HTTP/2 client could exhaust daemon memory by declaring a large number of fields in a `Trailer` header, bypassing the header size limits. [golang/go#81857](https://go.dev/issue/81857)
- **CVE-2026-78663**: An HTTP/2 client could bypass the connection-level flow control limit by resetting streams, making the daemon buffer more request data than the limit allows. [golang/go#81743](https://go.dev/issue/81743)
- **CVE-2026-78669**: An HTTP/2 client could cause excessive daemon CPU use by opening many streams and repeatedly changing the initial window size. [golang/go#81742](https://go.dev/issue/81742)
- **CVE-2026-56857**: On Windows, the daemon could create a directory outside its data root if someone with write access to the data root had placed a junction there. [golang/go#81739](https://go.dev/issue/81739)

The `golang.org/x/net` update to v0.60.0 applies the same HTTP/2 fixes to the deprecated `/grpc` endpoint and to the gRPC server that BuildKit runs for frontend containers, such as images referenced by a `# syntax=` directive.

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- containerd image store: Add the `lazy-pull` daemon feature to control whether `docker pull` skips downloading layer content that the snapshotter already provides. Lazy pulls are enabled by default for known remote snapshotters (`nydus`, `overlaybd`, `soci`, `stargz`). [moby/moby#53877](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53877)
- containerd image store: Fix pulls skipping required layer blobs when unpacked layers already exist, leaving images runnable but incomplete for export or push. [moby/moby#53615](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53615)
- Fix `docker container create --name` reporting a misleading validation error mentioning invalid characters instead of invalid name length. [moby/moby#53484](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53484)
- Fix a connection leak to the RootlessKit API socket on every `GET /version` request in rootless mode. [moby/moby#53836](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53836)
- Improve Windows service registration and unregistration cleanup, including making service unregistration (`--unregister-service`) idempotent. [moby/moby#53845](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53845)

##### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.34.0](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.34.0). [moby/moby#53882](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53882)
- Update Go runtime to [1.26.9](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.26.9). [docker/cli#7363](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7363)
- Update containerd (static binaries) to [v2.4.1](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.4.1). [moby/moby#53773](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53773)

##### Networking

- Allow IPv6 Neighbour Discovery between containers on a bridge network with inter-container communication disabled, matching the existing IPv4 behaviour. [moby/moby#53723](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53723)
- Fix `docker ps` and `GET /containers/json` omitting published ports for networks using routed gateway mode. [moby/moby#53693](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53693)
- Fix a bug where a restarted daemon could be dropped from a peer's service discovery and load balancing until it rejoined the gossip cluster. [moby/moby#53688](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53688)
- Fix a published port being unreachable from another container on the same network when inter-container communication is disabled, including Swarm services published through the routing mesh. [moby/moby#53723](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53723)
- Fix an issue where errors programming the kernel to encrypt the overlay network data-plane could in some circumstances lead to encrypted-overlay-network traffic to some nodes being transmitted in cleartext. As the receiving peer would drop cleartext packets for encrypted overlay networks as spoofed, the loss of confidentiality is limited to unidirectional flows (e.g. UDP DNS queries) and handshake attempts that never proceed (e.g. TCP SYN). [moby/moby#53420](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53420)
- Fix connecting live-restored containers with an implicit `host-gateway` mapping to additional networks. [moby/moby#53093](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53093)
- Fix overlay peers becoming unreachable after a node rejoins the cluster or a service is redeployed, when the VXLAN device had already learned a dynamic FDB entry for the peer. [moby/moby#53663](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53663)
- Fix Swarm tasks on overlay networks being rejected when the daemon can't write to `/var/lib/docker`. [moby/moby#53848](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53848)
- Published Swarm-service ports are accessible at the host's IPv6 addresses when the userland proxy is enabled. A change introduced in v29.8.0 incidentally enabled this functionality; it is a tested and supported feature as of v29.9.0. [moby/moby#53727](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53727)
- Release a node's IPsec security associations and policies when the last container leaves an encrypted overlay network, instead of leaking them until the daemon restarts. [moby/moby#53420](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53420)
- Restore the logic to remove the empty `DOCKER-INGRESS` iptables chain, and the `FORWARD` rule that jumps to it, left behind by Docker Engine 28.0.0 and earlier. [moby/moby#53825](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53825)

##### Rootless

- Update RootlessKit (3.2.0). [moby/moby#53607](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53607)

### [`v29.8.2`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.8.2): v29.8.2

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.8.1...docker-v29.8.2)

##### 29.8.2

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.8.2 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.8.2)
- [moby/moby, 29.8.2 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.8.2)

##### Security

This release fixes the following security vulnerabilities in Docker Engine:

- **CVE-2026-53493**: Pulling a crafted OCI image index with deeply nested or widely fanned-out descriptors could cause unbounded CPU and memory use. [GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-pg57-6jwg-q645)
- **CVE-2026-92543**: A malicious DNS response could make registry connections skip TLS certificate verification or fall back to HTTP, exposing registry credentials or allowing image substitution. [GHSA-7cfq-22r6-qp73](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-7cfq-22r6-qp73)
- **CVE-2026-92542**: Unprivileged users on a Swarm node could inject forged Ethernet frames into encrypted overlay networks on peer nodes. [GHSA-6m9p-4h64-m6vh](https://github.com/moby/moby/security/advisories/GHSA-6m9p-4h64-m6vh)

The BuildKit update fixes the following security vulnerabilities:

- **CVE-2026-93315**: A build step could redirect proxy CA cleanup outside the build root filesystem, block it with a special file, or let the build succeed when cleanup failed. [GHSA-2f5p-x9ph-g97x](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-2f5p-x9ph-g97x)
- **CVE-2026-93316**: A build that requested CDI devices could cause a daemon panic when CDI support was disabled, for example with `"features": {"cdi": false}` in `daemon.json`. [GHSA-r456-g3gm-cvxf](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-r456-g3gm-cvxf)
- **CVE-2026-93317**: With the containerd image store, a client using the low-level LLB API could poison the build cache with container blob contents that did not match their claimed digest. [GHSA-p3rc-w3hc-pqvv](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-p3rc-w3hc-pqvv)
- **CVE-2026-93318**: A malicious image could poison the build cache with layer DiffIDs that did not match the actual layer contents. [GHSA-f2v9-hprr-32q3](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-f2v9-hprr-32q3)
- **CVE-2026-93319**: A malicious external frontend could crash the daemon through gateway container lifecycle races or malformed requests and definitions. [GHSA-4hgw-qrhw-fhg8](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-4hgw-qrhw-fhg8)
- **CVE-2026-93320**: Daemon-side snapshot reads and LLB `mkfile` operations did not safely handle special files. [GHSA-9728-qjrv-2xh2](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-9728-qjrv-2xh2)
- **CVE-2026-93321**: A malformed LLB file operation with invalid symlink owner inputs could crash the daemon. [GHSA-fjj4-h6vf-m9hj](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-fjj4-h6vf-m9hj)
- **CVE-2026-93322**: A malformed LLB merge operation with mismatched input counts could crash the daemon. [GHSA-cv6p-7w7g-xjwq](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-cv6p-7w7g-xjwq)
- **CVE-2026-93323**: An oversized Dockerfile, `.dockerignore`, gateway file, or nested LLB definition could exhaust daemon memory. [GHSA-mgqf-486f-49vp](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-mgqf-486f-49vp)
- **CVE-2026-93326**: A crafted Git build source could bypass source policy rules that match on the repository URL, through a Git bundle locator or a full remote URL that did not match the source identifier. [GHSA-66hf-6vf5-87hc](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/security/advisories/GHSA-66hf-6vf5-87hc)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Fix `docker cp` failing on a container with a bind-mounted socket nested inside another bind mount. [moby/moby#53724](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53724)
- Fix `docker info` failing with an “invalid Prefix” error after reloading a daemon with custom default address pools. [moby/moby#53812](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53812)

##### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.33.1](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.33.1). [moby/moby#53823](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53823)
- Update containerd (static binaries) to [v2.3.6](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.6). [moby/moby#53778](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53778)
- Update runc (in static binaries) to [v1.5.2](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/tag/v1.5.2). [moby/moby#53811](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53811)

### [`v29.8.1`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.8.1): v29.8.1

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.8.0-rc.1...docker-v29.8.1)

##### 29.8.1

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.8.1 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.8.1)
- [moby/moby, 29.8.1 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.8.1)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- containerd image store: Fix `docker load` leaving dangling images after loading an image that already exists. [moby/moby#53595](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53595)
- Fix managed containerd logging a CRI pod-sandbox plugin dependency warning during startup. [moby/moby#53585](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53585)
- Fix user-namespace detection on OpenVZ, where namespace inode numbers are virtualized. [moby/moby#53605](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53605)
- Windows: Preserve hard links when committing a container, so a file with multiple names is stored once in the resulting image layer instead of once per name. [moby/moby#53624](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53624)

##### Packaging updates

- Update containerd (static binaries) to [v2.3.5](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.5). [moby/moby#53589](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53589)

##### Networking

- Fix `GET /networks` returning a 500 status if an invalid 'type' filter was provided. [moby/moby#53678](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53678)

### [`v29.8.0`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.8.0): v29.8.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.7.2...docker-v29.8.0-rc.1)

#### 29.8.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.8.0 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.8.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.8.0 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.8.0)

##### New

- Add `HostConfig.Umask` option and a corresponding `--umask <octal>` flag to `docker create`/`docker run` to set the umask for a container's main process, execs, and healthchecks. [moby/moby#53463](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53463), [docker/cli#7108](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7108)
- Add support for attaching service names, environments, and custom CloudWatch entity attributes to logs from the `awslogs` logging driver. [moby/moby#52632](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52632)

##### Security

- Add daemon support for configuring the default container AppArmor profile template. [moby/moby#52771](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52771)
  - See <https://docker.docker.com/engine/security/apparmor/#customize-the-default-profile>
- Prevent containers from using the 32-bit `socketcall(2)` path to create `AF_VSOCK` sockets and communicate with host virtual machines by adding AppArmor and SELinux policy rules. [moby/moby#53551](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53551)

##### Networking

- Fix `docker network inspect` failing to find a healthy Swarm network when another Swarm network could not be allocated. [moby/moby#53325](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53325)
- Fix a node gossiping a superseded value for a Swarm service discovery entry after concurrent updates to the same key. [moby/moby#53479](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53479)
- Fix Swarm service names failing to resolve on a node indefinitely after it misses a network membership announcement. [moby/moby#53437](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53437)
- Fix Swarm service names failing to resolve on healthy nodes after a transient node failure. [moby/moby#53142](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53142)
- Prevent dockerd from hanging when the nft command produces enough stderr output to fill its pipe. [moby/moby#53517](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53517)
- Reduce gossip traffic generated by a node that repeatedly disconnects and rejoins the cluster. [moby/moby#53479](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53479)
- Remote network-driver plugins can now set the container-side interface name via the `DstName` field in their `Join` response. [moby/moby#52866](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52866)
- Reserve network names "container" and "container:" to prevent creation of unusable networks. [moby/moby#51973](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/51973)
- Spread the daemon's periodic Swarm overlay network gossip and synchronization work over time, avoiding recurring bursts of CPU and network usage. [moby/moby#53475](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53475)
- Swarm service-mesh published ports now use the same infrastructure as published ports for local containers. [moby/moby#53118](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53118)

##### Rootless

- Fix `--disable-host-loopback` not being enforced for the `pasta` network driver in rootless mode. [moby/moby#53358](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53358)
- Update RootlessKit to v3.1.0, adding support for the `pesto` port driver in rootless mode. Set `DOCKERD_ROOTLESS_ROOTLESSKIT_PORT_DRIVER=pesto` to use it; it requires the `pasta` network driver and supports IPv4 only. [moby/moby#53358](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53358)

##### Go SDK

- Update minimum supported Go version to 1.26. [docker/cli#7258](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7258)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Add `annotation` filter to container listings (`docker ps`, `GET /containers/json`) allowing to filter containers by their annotations. [moby/moby#53538](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53538)
- containerd image store: Fix `docker image inspect` reporting a smaller image size than `docker image ls`. [moby/moby#53426](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53426)
- containerd image store: Fix slower image pulls caused by repeated registry authentication within a single pull. [moby/moby#53497](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53497)
- Do not log expected image signature identity misses as errors for containerd image store images. [moby/moby#53495](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53495)
- dockerd now uses the embedded containerd if no system containerd service is configured and containerd is not installed. [moby/moby#53388](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53388)
- Fix `GET /images/{name}/json` not including unpacked snapshot usage in `Size` when using the containerd image store. [moby/moby#53426](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53426)
- Fix classic-builder cache for Dockerfile stages that select a non-host platform with `FROM --platform`. [moby/moby#53503](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53503)
- Fix CLI panic when `DOCKER_HOST` or `-H` specifies an invalid host. [docker/cli#7280](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7280)
- Fix health checks being delayed for too long when the start interval is longer than the start period. [moby/moby#52317](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52317)
- Fix inconsistent mount ordering in `docker inspect` output (`GET /containers/{id}/json`) and container listings (`docker ps`, `GET /containers/json`). [moby/moby#53534](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53534)
- Fix NRI container metadata so `Container.Args` includes the resolved executable as `argv[0]`, matching the process launched in the container instead of only the Docker `Cmd`. [moby/moby#53423](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53423)
- Fix Swarm service creation failing when an automatically generated name is already in use. [moby/moby#53468](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53468)
- Fix the container root directory `/` being world-writable when using the `btrfs` storage driver. [moby/moby#53500](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53500)
- Fixed `docker ps` sorting published ports lexicographically instead of numerically. [docker/cli#7144](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7144)
- Preserve service mount order during forced updates to avoid an unnecessary rollout on the next stack deploy. [docker/cli#7227](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7227)
- Prevent containerd's v2 CRI plugins from loading when CRI is disabled. [moby/moby#53564](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53564)
- Print plugin hook output (e.g. the "What's next:" hint) after the command's error message instead of before it. [docker/cli#6976](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/6976)
- Reject checkpoint IDs containing path separators to prevent access outside the container checkpoint directory. [moby/moby#53377](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53377)

##### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.33.0](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.33.0). [moby/moby#53554](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53554)
- Update containerd (static binaries) to [v2.3.4](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.4). [moby/moby#53409](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53409)
- Update Go runtime to [1.26.8](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.26.8). [moby/moby#53550](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53550), [docker/cli#7274](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7274)
- Update runc (in static binaries) to [v1.5.1](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/tag/v1.5.1). [moby/moby#52306](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52306)

### [`v29.7.2`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.7.2): v29.7.2

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.7.1...docker-v29.7.2)

##### 29.7.2

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.7.2 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.7.2)
- [moby/moby, 29.7.2 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.7.2)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Fix `docker service create` and `docker service update` panicking when the same environment variable is passed more than once. [docker/cli#7145](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7145)
- Fix a regression introduced in Docker Engine 29.7.0 that caused image pulls to reject images containing absolute hardlink targets, as produced by some image builders. [moby/moby#53305](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53305)
- Fix a regression introduced in Docker Engine 29.7.0 that could cause image pulls and `docker cp` to fail on older Linux kernels when applying file permissions, including for device nodes. [moby/moby#53305](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53305)

##### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.32.2](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.32.2). [moby/moby#53300](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53300)

##### Networking

- Improve compatibility with more nftables releases by terminating base-chain policies with a semicolon. [moby/moby#53303](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53303)

### [`v29.7.1`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.7.1): v29.7.1

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.7.0-rc.1...docker-v29.7.1)

##### 29.7.1

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.7.1 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.7.1)
- [moby/moby, 29.7.1 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.7.1)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Fix a regression that prevented pulling images whose layers contain directories without explicit parent directory entries. [moby/moby#53260](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53260)
- Fix a regression where the `CopyToContainer` rejects container paths that traverse absolute symlinks, such as `/var/run` -> `/run`. [moby/moby#53261](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53261)

### [`v29.7.0`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.7.0): v29.7.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.6.2...docker-v29.7.0-rc.1)

##### 29.7.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.7.0 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.7.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.7.0 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.7.0)

##### New

- Add an experimental `embedded-containerd` feature that runs containerd inside the daemon process instead of as a separate managed process. [moby/moby#52898](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52898)
- Mount type `image` is no longer experimental. [moby/moby#52998](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52998)
- Add the `default-stop-timeout` daemon option to configure the stop timeout assigned to containers without an explicit timeout. [moby/moby#53146](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53146)

##### Security

This release includes a fix for a security vulnerability affecting Docker Engine and related components.

- Update github.com/moby/go-archive to v0.3.0 to fix [CVE-2026-17106](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-17106) / [GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h](https://github.com/moby/go-archive/security/advisories/GHSA-hfg8-hc9c-6c3h). [moby/moby#53247](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53247), [docker/cli#7139](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7139)

##### Networking

- Fix a daemon panic when cleanup of a container's network interface fails while the container is being disconnected from a network. [moby/moby#53237](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53237)
- Fix a daemon panic when removing swarm ingress ports after failing to bind an ingress proxy listener. [moby/moby#53022](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53022)

##### Rootless

- Keep the cgroup mount for containers with `--net=host`. [moby/moby#52318](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52318)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Add shell completion for `--filter` names and known values to `docker service ls`, `docker service ps`, and `docker node ps`. [docker/cli#7124](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7124)
- containerd image store: Fix daemon-wide concurrent download and upload limits for pulls and pushes not being honored. [moby/moby#53081](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53081)
  - To preserve the previous unlimited startup behavior, configure "max-concurrent-downloads" and "max-concurrent-uploads" to 0
- Fix `docker cp -a` using the wrong file owner when copying files into containers with user namespace remapping enabled. [moby/moby#53084](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53084)
- Fix `docker cp` from a Windows container silently returning a file instead of an error when the source path ends with a separator but is not a directory. [moby/moby#53123](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53123)
- Fix `docker stats` reporting all zeros for running Windows containers when using the containerd runtime. [moby/moby#53101](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53101)
- Fix `docker stats` reporting empty network stats for running Windows containers when using the containerd runtime. [moby/moby#53219](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53219)
- Fix a typo in the `docker create --pull` flag description. [docker/cli#7103](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7103)
- Fix Swarm service updates failing due to "file exists" errors when a VIP IP alias already exists on the LB endpoint interface. [moby/moby#51657](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/51657)
- Fix Swarm tasks being rejected when their image could not be pulled from the registry but was already present on the node. [moby/moby#53212](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53212)
- Improve the error returned when a container hostname exceeds Linux's 64-byte limit. [moby/moby#53121](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53121)
- Prevent live-restored volumes from retaining active mount references when containers exit during daemon startup. [moby/moby#53115](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53115)
- Suppress the “No such container” error when `docker rm --force` succeeds for a nonexistent container. [docker/cli#7110](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7110)

##### Packaging updates

- Update Go runtime to [1.26.5](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.26.5). [docker/cli#7087](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7087)
- Update BuildKit to [v0.32.0](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.32.0). [moby/moby#53234](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53234)
- Update containerd (static binaries) to [v2.3.3](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.3.3). [moby/moby#53050](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53050)
- Update runc (in static binaries) to [v1.4.3](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/tag/v1.4.3). [moby/moby#50960](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/50960)

body:
0.10.4 stages the kit on a fresh inode so it inherits the destination directory's ACL, then stamps it with the storage's own mode. On an ACL-backed share the stamp undoes the staging: any `chmod` there discards the inherited ACL, including a `chmod` to the mode the file already carries.

Observed on a Synology volume backing a `local` target. The two views disagree:

| | inside the container | on the host |
|---|---|---|
| `config` | `700`, no ACL visible | `777+`, ACL grants the mirror user |
| freshly created file | `0` | `777+` (inherited) |

So the kit was chowned (ACL survives), then chmod'ed `700` onto a file already reading `700`, which dropped the ACL. Verification compared `700` to `700`, passed, and the placement was recorded as done — a kit the mirror user could not read, on a target archiver considered current. Confirmed by experiment on the share: `cp` inherits the ACL, `chown` preserves it, `chmod` destroys it.

The placement now chmods only when that would change the mode, so a file already matching the storage keeps whatever the directory granted it. A placement below the reference is still stamped up to it, unchanged.

The SFTP path is deliberately untouched: there the mode reads back as the ACL-synthesized `777` and already matches, and applying the same skip rule would collide with `recovery_kit_sftp_mode` treating a bare `0` as unreadable, producing a permanent re-upload loop.

`RECOVERY_KIT_STATE_VERSION` is bumped to 5 so existing deployments re-place their kit once after upgrade.

Tests: two new cases in `tests/recovery_kit.bats` (no chmod when the mode already matches; still chmod'ed up when it does not). Full suite 88/88.

body:
The v0.10.5 tag run went red on **Workflow summary** with `github_failures: 15`. Build-and-push and reconcile both succeeded and the new release was created on all three registries; what failed was a contiguous band of PATCHes to *old* GitHub releases — `v0.8.4` down to `v0.5.0`, with the 18 newer and 11 older ones fine. The v0.10.4 tag run (4194) failed identically, so this has been red for at least two releases.

The cause is still unknown, and that is the point: `reconcile_release` ran `curl -fsSL -X PATCH ... >/dev/null` and printed a bare `update FAILED`, discarding the status code and GitHub's message. Replaying all 15 PATCHes by hand with the identical payload returned `200` every time, and 30 rapid PATCHes provoked no secondary rate limit, so there is nothing to go on after the fact.

Three changes:

**Write only what differs.** The loop revisits every tag on every run, so each release rewrote all 43 releases on all three registries — ~129 writes per run, growing with the tag list, re-sending content that last changed when the tag was cut. `release_matches` compares `{name, body, draft, prerelease}` and skips the PATCH when they are equal. Verified against live data on all three hosts: the stored bodies are byte-identical to what the workflow generates, so a run now makes ~3 writes instead of ~129. `target_commitish` is deliberately excluded — it cannot change for an existing tag, and a host that echoed a branch name instead of the sha would make every release look stale.

**Report the failure.** `api_write` keeps the status code and the first 400 characters of the response body in `API_WRITE_ERROR`, so the next real failure is diagnosable from the log instead of being lost.

**Retry the transient classes.** Up to three attempts on `429`/`5xx` and on GitHub's secondary-rate-limit `403`, never on a genuine permission `403`. The server's `Retry-After` wins over the local 10s/20s ladder when it asks for longer (bounded at 120s; an HTTP-date value falls back to the ladder), since retrying inside an active rate-limit window can extend it.

Two findings from an independent review are folded in: honouring `Retry-After`, and re-checking by tag after a failed *create* — a POST is not idempotent, so a 5xx returned after the host already committed the release would turn the retry into a 409/422 and report failure for a release that exists and is correct.

Tested against a mock API. Attempt counts: `200` → 1, real `403` → 1, `404` → 1, `503` → 3, secondary-rate `403` → 3. `Retry-After: 45` produced 90s of backoff where the ladder would have given 30s; an HTTP-date `Retry-After` fell back to 30s. A POST that 5xx'd after committing was recovered and reported as `created (confirmed after a retried create)`. Negative tests: a changed body, a changed name, a flipped `prerelease`, and malformed JSON from the host all fall through to a write. Shellcheck clean, YAML parses.

Note this job only runs on tag pushes, so PR CI does not exercise it — the next release is the first real run.

Records the ground-up refactor's compatibility policy and the four Phase 1 gate decisions, one ADR each:

- 0001: v1.0.0 compatibility policy. Never break storages, snapshot IDs, encryption keys, restoring old snapshots, or plain-openssl kit recovery; everything else may change with a migration command and an upgrade guide.
- 0002: cross-version compatibility tests before rewrite code.
- 0003: patch the audit's safety findings in bash first, each with a failing test.
- 0004: drop bundle mode in v1, after a tested migration.
- 0005: refactor backlog scope.

Docs only; no runtime change and no CHANGELOG entry (not user-facing).

body:
MinIO's community image (`minio/minio`) is gone from Docker Hub, so `tests/integration/s3-minio.sh` fails in the host-driven CI job on every PR (including Renovate's and #105), and the sftp and entrypoint-secrets tests after it never run.

This swaps the fixture for Garage v2.3.0 (the NAS's exact pin), single-node with a caller-chosen key and `root_domain` for virtual-host buckets, behind a Caddy 2.11.4 sidecar that terminates TLS (duplicacy's `s3://` backend is https-only). Same production path and the same assertions as before: backup over `s3://`, the recovery kit as a plain object readable with SigV4 path-style, and restore with content checks. Readiness waits for a signed ListObjectsV2 to return 200.

Verified on a real Docker daemon: s3-garage passes (38s), and so do the other host-driven tests (sigterm-stop, invalid-cron, sftp-runtime, entrypoint-secrets) plus roundtrip. Test-only change; no CHANGELOG entry.
head: refs/pull/106/head
title: test: run the s3 integration test against Garage instead of MinIO

body:
The ADR 3 safety patch: fixes from the Phase 1 audit, one commit each. Every fix started with an integration test that failed on the current image.

1. **Hooks**: the post-backup hook always runs once the pre-backup hook has (after a failed backup or a stop too), a failed pre hook skips that service's backup instead of reporting success, a failed post hook or unparseable settings file is an error, and no further service starts after a stop.
2. **Credentials**: `duplicacy set -value` wrote the storage password, RSA passphrase, and B2/S3 keys in plaintext into every service directory's `.duplicacy/preferences` and onto argv. They now go only through `DUPLICACY_<NAME>_*` env vars (RSA passphrase exported; a storage named `default` uses duplicacy's unprefixed names).
3. **SERVICE_DIRECTORIES**: entries matching no directory, paths containing a space (were word-split), and names that cannot form a snapshot ID are reported as errors instead of skipped silently.
4. **Image build**: duplicacy, supercronic, and the docker CLI are verified against pinned per-arch SHA-256s; a CI lint enforces it. Renovate bumps of these three now need their digests updated by hand (the build fails closed until then).
5. **README**: the Kubernetes CronJob example sets a stable pod hostname.

Behavior changes worth noting at release: runs that silently skipped data or ignored a failed pre hook now exit non-zero. The nas and vps hooks all return 0 by design, so they are unaffected.

Verified on a Docker daemon: 28/28 integration tests and 91 bats pass on the head; each commit got a Codex review.

Phase 4, ADR 2: every contract behavior Cody marked is now a Go black-box e2e test (six groups, written and independently verified by a 12-agent workflow; each test proven by a sabotaged image). The tests found four real 0.11 defects, fixed here as the 0.11.1 patch (tests land first, per the patch-release rule):

- security: hooks inherited the DUPLICACY_* storage password / RSA passphrase (every post hook, every later pre hook)
- restore without CHOWN/FOWNER aborted at the first non-root file (the warn-not-refuse promise was false)
- a stopped backup could exit 0 (stop handler killed by its own signal); a stopped maintenance run exited 0
- the recovery kit was named by the kernel hostname, not the inherited HOSTNAME (a new kit per Job pod)

Dropped by Cody: making the healthcheck unhealthy after a failed finished run (deliberate old behavior; revisit in Phase 6b).

Also: pause-resume.sh polls instead of a fixed 3s sleep (flaked under load).

Local: 29/29 e2e on the fixed image (the four bug tests fail on 0.11.0), bats 91/91, old integration suite green, shellcheck clean, Codex review clean.

body:
ADR 9 prerequisite, before main takes its first breaking change.

- `release.yml`: new `alpha` bump; version and branch rules move to `.forgejo/scripts/next-version.sh` (bats: `tests/next_version.bats`, 8 cases). main cuts 0.x until its first 1.0.0 alpha, then alphas and 1.0.0 (and 1.x again once 1.0.0 ships); `release/<major>.<minor>` cuts only that line's patches, counting only tags reachable from HEAD. Alphas skip the compose/README/guide image bump.
- `docker-publish.yml`: prerelease tags skip the version-refs check and are created as prereleases on all three release hosts; no `latest` tag was ever pushed and metadata-action already skips major/minor tags for prereleases. PRs to `release/**` get CI. The bats job runs the pinned image with git added (Renovate-tracked via the inline `# renovate:` convention).

After merge, `release/0.11` must be fast-forwarded to main so its own workflow copy has these paths (possible while main has no breaking change).

Local: bats 98/98 (CI-equivalent run), shellcheck clean, yamllint clean, Codex review clean after one real fix (post-1.0 patches were blocked).

body:
First Go code in the image. `/usr/local/bin/archiver` becomes a static Go binary (cross-compiled in a pinned golang stage, CGO off) that execs `archiver.sh` for every command, or `lib/scripts/init.sh` for `init` (archiver.sh has no init verb). exec replaces the process, so signals, the TTY, and exit codes pass through unchanged. The entrypoint's crontab, SIGTERM stop, run mode, and init now call the dispatcher (ADR 8 consequence), so a ported command will also cover scheduled runs and shutdown.

Small visible changes: usage says `archiver` instead of the script path; `archiver init` works inside a running container.

This is main's first change past 0.11 (ADR 9): from here 0.11 patches come from `release/0.11`.

Second commit: a Go CI job (gofmt, go vet, go test -race) that publishing waits on.

Local: 28/28 integration and 29/29 e2e on the built image, invalid-cron + scheduler rerun after updating their crontab assertions (a real Codex catch), Go job dry-run green, Codex review clean.

title: feat(cli): Go dispatcher for archiver (ADR 8 step zero)

body:
Cody's decisions of 2026-09-29, after the NAS skipped the 09-28 backup behind a long copy, an ISP outage failed both copies with no retry, and local accumulated 2.17 TiB of orphaned fossils from ghost-snapshot races.

- 0011: a copy worker per target (targets in parallel, one all-snapshot copy at a time per target, backoff retries until caught up; backup lock covers only the local backup).
- 0012: targets mirror local retention (only local runs -keep; guarded deletions on targets).
- 0013: built in the Go pipeline port next, with a refused-backup alert in bash meanwhile.

Text approved by Cody; Codex review surfaced two real gaps (mirroring must also trigger on local prunes; bash maintenance must stop pruning targets when mirroring ships), both folded in. A third Codex claim (per-ID partial visibility in an all-ID copy) was rejected: duplicacy_main calls CopySnapshots once and it writes all snapshot files after all chunks.
head: refs/pull/117/head
title: docs(adr): offsite-resilience decisions (ADRs 0011-0013)

body:
ADR 10 step 1. Five commits: a read-only reader for the bash lock files and maintenance record, then status, healthcheck, logs, and the dispatcher wiring (ported commands run in Go when called with no arguments; anything else still goes to archiver.sh, so usage errors are unchanged).

- status and healthcheck: byte-identical output and exit codes to bash in four states (fresh, after a real backup, after maintenance, finished-with-error), checked in a container. The deliberate finished-but-failed-stays-healthy rule is kept; config.sh is read as plain assignments, never executed (ADR 4).
- logs: follows in-process; Ctrl+C exits in ~1 ms with 130 and leaves no background tail (backlog item), SIGTERM exits 143, follows log rotation, exits 0 when the backup ends. Drops tail's ==> file <== headers.
- CI Go job now covers internal/; Dockerfile copies internal/ into the build stage.

Local: go test -race green, every commit builds and tests on its own, 28/28 integration + 29/29 e2e on the built image, Codex review clean after fixes (SIGTERM status, logo newline, CHANGELOG wording); one Codex point rejected (sourcing config.sh would violate ADR 4; bundle mode has no live users).

Test first: TestRunsRefusedBackupNotifies fails on 0.11.1 (no notification in 30s) and passes with the fix. The e2e runner also gets an explicit 30-minute timeout (go test's 10-minute default failed the suite on a busy runner; same fix is in #118 for main).

body:
ADRs 11, 15, 16 (check intervals, mirroring and target maintenance come next).

- Under the daemon (BACKUP_SCHEDULE set), one copy worker per secondary, each with its own copy repository prepared in its first pass: copies every revision its target lacks, one copy at a time, targets in parallel; retries at 1/5/15 min then every 30, with one retry landing on the 30-minute mark where the target is declared down (one notification, a daily reminder, one on recovery). State persists in logs/.copy-workers.json; status shows it; logs/copies.log.
- A backup hands its copies off over the daemon socket and ends; without a daemon (or with different storage settings than the daemon's) it copies inline as before, under the same per-target copy lock. Forced-bash backups are refused while workers run.
- stop/pause/resume reach the workers (bash scripts call `archiver daemon ctl`).
- Safety: per-storage kernel lock around every init/add (duplicacy 3.2.5 has no create-if-absent), per-target copy lock shared by workers and inline copies, daemon ownership lock, stop generations against races, shutdown cancels passes.
- Backups never contact a secondary in steady state: registrations are carried over from the previous preferences (credentials stripped) while the URL is unchanged; first-time registration is bounded (5 min) and skipped for targets the workers report failing. Recovery-kit step: skips failing secondaries, exit 3 for secondary-only failures (not a handed-off backup's failure), 30 min deadline excluding paused time, own process group.
- Also: fix log rotation for two runs in the same second; fix the lock-release race behind lock-concurrency's intermittent CI failure.

Known residuals: a brand-new secondary is contacted once on first registration; maintenance can fail once for a secondary registered while its worker was still preparing (target maintenance moves into the workers next).

body:
ADR 24: the recovery kit reaches every storage through a bundled, checksum-pinned rclone (v1.75.1, Renovate-tracked) instead of per-type curl/sftp code.

- Credentials go to rclone only in its environment (`RCLONE_CONFIG_KIT_*`, `--config /dev/null`), never argv or disk.
- The kit is placed only beside an existing storage (its Duplicacy `config` must be at the destination): rclone would otherwise create a missing directory and report success for an unmounted path or mistyped bucket.
- `--ignore-times`: a kit chosen for upload is always sent (equal size and coarse timestamps would skip a changed kit and leave the old one marked current).
- SFTP: `set_modtime=false` (servers refusing SETSTAT), no remote shell, host keys trusted on first use as before, and only the key types already trusted are offered (otherwise rclone negotiates another type and calls it a changed key).
- Local and SFTP permission matching is kept (owner/mode of the storage's config, chmod only when it differs, verified or kept out of the state).
- Existing kits stay current: same content, name, state.

Tests (each new one confirmed failing without its fix): sftp-runtime gains a server refusing SETSTAT and a known_hosts with one of several key types; unit tests for credentials off argv, local placement, trusted algorithms. Local: all integration tests, full e2e.

Now: transient failures (network errors, 429, 5xx) are retried after 5s and 10s, with a 15s attempt timeout, so a send ends within about a minute. A refusal such as bad credentials is not retried and still says to check the Pushover secrets.

Unit tests cover retry-then-success, exhausted retries, a dropped connection and no retry on 400.

body:
Maintenance ran check and prune from the first service directory with a repository. Duplicacy keeps a prune's pending fossil collections in that repository's cache, so adding a service that sorts first stranded them: their chunks waited for the next exhaustive prune. (V1 checklist, Phase 4 leftover.)

Now:
- Maintenance uses `logs/.maintenance-repo/`, beside the copy workers' repositories (same logs-mount advice in the README).
- A `storages` identities file (written atomically) drops the cache of a storage removed or repointed since, as the copy workers do by hashing names into their repository paths.
- Each run takes over collections that service repositories hold for the same storage name and URL. They are moved (not copied) and renumbered after the repository's own, so the upgrade from 0.11 keeps them.
- The primary is registered first. Each secondary is registered only at its turn, so one that hangs cannot hold up the primary, and one that cannot be registered fails on its own. Registration ends on `archiver stop` or a signal.
- Maintenance no longer refuses to run before the first backup. It also closes the loose end "a newly registered secondary fails maintenance once", since maintenance now registers storages itself.

Tests:
- e2e `TestRunsFossilsKeptForNewService` was red on main in both cases: a collection made by this image (logs mounted), and one left by the 0.11 baseline and taken over on upgrade.
- e2e `TestRunsMaintenanceGoesOnPastBadSecondary`.
- Unit tests for the collection takeover and the identities file.
- Locally green: all maintenance, prune and cross-version e2e tests.

Review (Codex): accepted findings on worker-owned secondaries, stop-awareness, registering secondaries at their turn and the atomic identities write. Rejected maintaining secondaries when the primary cannot be registered: adding a secondary without `-copy <primary> -bit-identical` could create a storage that is not bit-identical (never-break).

title: fix: maintenance runs from its own repository

body:
A restore already refused to start during a backup, but a backup could start mid-restore and save a half-restored service directory. (V1 checklist loose end; it was there in 0.11 too.)

Now:
- A restore whose destination is, lies in or holds a service directory holds `/var/lock/archiver-restore.lock` until the command ends, its restore hook included.
- A backup probes that lock with its own already held, and the restore checks for a running backup after taking it, so whichever starts second sees the other. A refused backup exits 1 and notifies "Backup Skipped". If the probe errors, the backup refuses rather than assume no restore.
- Overlap is judged against the backup's own expansion of SERVICE_DIRECTORIES, symlinks resolved on both sides, after the destination is created. Pattern fallbacks cover service directories the restore will create below it (wildcard-matched symlinks included). Bracket classes it cannot match exactly count as overlapping, so the guard errs toward keeping backups out.
- Restores elsewhere (a DR test into /tmp) only check that no backup is running, as before.
- duplicacy children inherit the lock, so one that outlives a killed restore still keeps backups out. The restore hook does not inherit it, because a service it starts in the background would hold the lock indefinitely.

Known limit: if archiver is killed (SIGTERM/SIGKILL) while a post-restore hook runs, the hook can outlive the lock. Closing that needs a supervising process; logged as a follow-up, not done here.

Tests:
- e2e `TestRunsBackupRefusedDuringRestore` was red on main (the backup ran during the restore) and is green here.
- Unit tests for the guard (symlinks, missing service directories, wildcard-symlink ancestors, conservative bracket classes) and an updated `TestAutoAll`.
- Locally green: every TestRuns, Restore and CrossVersion e2e test, plus all 27 round-trip integration scripts.

Review (Codex, several passes): accepted path normalization, missing service directories, glob semantics, relative patterns, fail-closed probe, the unconditional backup recheck and keeping the hook from inheriting the lock. Rejected only the supervising-process ask (see Known limit).

body:
Phase 4 leftover, per Cody's decision (2026-10-08): default 2, `BACKUP_PARALLELISM` configurable, 1 keeps today's one-by-one order.

- Each service runs its pre-backup hook, backup and post-backup hook. Up to `BACKUP_PARALLELISM` services run at once.
- Directories sharing a snapshot ID (listed twice, or two with one name) and one directory under two names (a symlink) go one after another, in order. Two backups of one snapshot ID never run at once (never-break), and two never share one `.duplicacy` repository at once.
- With 1, everything runs in the configured order exactly.
- After a stop, no further service starts; running ones end as before (new e2e test).
- Inline copies still run from the last successful service in configured order.
- Shared pipeline state (old preferences per service, failing-target list) is behind the mutex.
- Notifications: sends are serialized, so concurrent alerts all arrive instead of the second being dropped. The anti-loop guard moved to the source: send outcomes are logged with the new `logging.Log.Unnotified`, so a failed send never notifies.
- The setting is recorded in the recovery kit (`IsSetting`) and validated (>= 1).
- Docs: README performance section, env example, CHANGELOG.

Tests: e2e `TestRunsServicesInParallel` (two hooks meet at a barrier by default; with 1 they never overlap) and `TestRunsStopStartsNoMoreServices`; unit tests for grouping, the setting, concurrent notifications and the no-loop wiring. Three integration scripts whose subject is one-by-one order now pin `BACKUP_PARALLELISM=1`. Locally green: TestRuns, ExitStop, Hooks and CrossVersion e2e, plus all 27 round-trip integration scripts.

Review (Codex) found and I fixed: same-snapshot-ID and same-repository concurrency, serial-mode order, and dropped concurrent notifications.

body:
Four fault-injection suites (ADR 31), in CI:

- fault-corruption.sh: chunks only revision 2 has are deleted/altered. Check names the damaged revision, fails and notifies; drill fails and notifies; restoring revision 2 fails; revision 1 restores byte for byte.
- fault-kill.sh: duplicacy, a pre-backup hook, archiver itself (SIGKILL), and a copy worker's copy are killed. Runs fail, post-backup still runs, locks are freed or cleared as stale, no revision added, the next run proceeds and restores; the worker retries and catches up.
- fault-disk.sh (host-driven, tmpfs mounts): full storage, full restore target and full logs volume each fail with a clear error and notification, and recover once space returns.
- fault-network.sh (host-driven, toxiproxy in front of SFTP): a slow link completes; a link cut mid-backup fails with no revision and frees the lock; a link cut mid-copy is retried (duplicacy's own backoff, then the worker) and never reported caught up; both recover and restore.

Defects found and fixed (each its own commit, test-first by the suites above):
1. An unwritable log never notified: every line failed to stdout only. Now notifies once a run.
2. Maintenance logged "Maintenance completed successfully" after a failed check or prune (exit code was right). The summary now counts errors, as backup's does.
3. A failed check did not say which revisions were damaged (duplicacy stops at the first). Checks run with -persist and the error and notification list "damaged revisions: ID revision N, ..." (maintenance and copy workers).

Noted, not changed: a plain check only proves chunks exist; bit rot inside a data chunk is found by drills (or check -chunks, which downloads everything).

ADR 40, release path only (build-and-push runs on tags):
- Build with `sbom: true` and `provenance: mode=max`; if the attested build fails, a second build without attestations runs and warns (attestations never fail a release).
- The OCI archive is pushed to one candidate tag (`release-candidate`); skopeo --digestfile records exactly what was pushed. cosign v3.0.2 signs that digest with the key from secrets (COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY/COSIGN_PASSWORD), `--use-signing-config=false --tlog-upload=false` (no Rekor; signature stored beside the image as the `sha256-<hex>` tag), verifies it against cosign.pub, and only then are the release tags set (copied from the signed digest). A missing secret or failed signature fails the job, so tags, mirrors and release notes never carry an unsigned image. Registry login goes to cosign through a per-run volume's config.json, not argv.
- NAS sync carries the signature tag; the GHCR mirror copies it explicitly.
- trivy 0.69.1 scans each release (continue-on-error) and the newest release weekly (scan-weekly.yml, SemVer-aware newest, exit 0).
- cosign.pub at the repo root; README "Verifying Images"; .renovaterc includePaths gains scan-weekly.yml; per-run volume names (also for the existing skopeo-stage).

Key: cosign key pair in OpenBao kvv2 projects/archiver/release-signing (version 2) and the two Forgejo repo secrets. Version 1 was retired before any use: a local dry run with cosign v3's default signing-config mode uploaded two test entries (alpine:3.20's digest, signed with that key) to public Rekor despite --tlog-upload=false; nothing secret was in them. The fix (--use-signing-config=false) was proven with a throwaway key: no Rekor entry.

- Release: build-and-push becomes a matrix over full/slim, max-parallel 1 (shared layers race Forgejo's blob uniqueness; both run the NAS sync); slim tags carry `-slim` (metadata-action suffix), its own candidate tag and per-variant volumes; signed like the full image. Mirror outcomes are set only on failure so one leg cannot overwrite the other's.
- PR CI: new `slim` job builds the slim target and runs tests/integration/slim-tools.sh (SLIM=1: essentials present, hook tools absent) and roundtrip, recovery-kit, envelope, restore-commands, maintenance, recover; integration checks the full image holds the hook tools (SLIM=0). build-and-push needs it.
- scan-weekly skips -slim tags when picking the newest release. README "Image Tags".

Local: slim-tools both ways, six scripts on slim, and all 52 integration scripts + e2e on the new full image pass (its essentials now come from the slim stage without recommends). Codex: 2 rounds, last clean.

- internal/config/reference.go: `Reference`, one table of every setting (group, secret, default, values, kind, description, case folding, schema pattern), plus `TargetReference()` built from the storage types' fields (with the breakglass secret variants and their types listed).
- reference_render.go: `ReferenceMarkdown()` -> docs/configuration.md; `ReferenceSchema()` -> docs/archiver.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12; empty always allowed as unset; enums, case-insensitive patterns only where the loader folds case; ECMA-262 patterns matching ParseInterval, port 1-65535, counts >= 1; a secret set as a variable is flagged `not: {}` with its `_FILE` alternative).
- Tests: every name the loader's settings/secrets patterns accept and every literal Getenv/getenv in internal/ and cmd/ is documented (allowlist: HOME, PATH, kit step markers, refused old names); the two files equal what the table generates (`UPDATE_REFERENCE=1 go test ./internal/config` rewrites them).
- Checked: schema validates under Draft 2020-12 (good env passes, bad env flagged); all 137 patterns compile as JS regexes; interval/port patterns behave as the parser does.
- README links both. Codex: 5 rounds, last clean.

body:
ADR 46 without the Duplicacy patch (that follows as its own PR: it touches how snapshots are written, so it gets its own design review and verification).

**57fd21d SIGINT on stop.** `proc.Spec.Interrupt`: Terminate sends INT and waits up to 30 s before TERM/KILL; set on every duplicacy spec (backup, copy, prune, check). Duplicacy 3.2.5 saves its resume point on INT (a hash-mode backup's incomplete snapshot, a check's verified chunks) and nothing on TERM. `stop --immediate` sends INT to duplicacy children (TERM to the rest). Copy workers terminate in the background, so stopping all workers never waits on one; the entrypoint's shutdown waits for the copy flocks too.

**a042d37 run records + catch-up.** `internal/resume`: logs/.run-{backup,maintenance,drill}.json, written aside + fsynced (and the directory) so a power cut after a pre hook still finds it. Backup stages per service: pending / hooked (pre ran, post not) / done. A backup starts by running each `hooked` service's post-backup hook with `ARCHIVER_BACKUP_RESULT=interrupted` (recorded at once, never twice), then backs up unfinished services first. `ARCHIVER_STATE_DIR` moved to logs/.hook-state/<snapshot id> so that post hook finds what pre left. Any normal end clears the record; a stop for a container shutdown (`archiver stop --shutdown`, the entrypoint's; flag cleared at start) keeps it. The daemon runs interrupted kinds once at start (`daemon.Run` catchUp: before the job's schedule, or alone if unscheduled); manual mode starts them from the entrypoint. A drill deletes the copies an interrupted drill recorded, only real `drill-*` dirs directly in the recorded root, outside service dirs, with nothing mounted at or under them.

Tests: tests/integration/fault-interrupt.sh (new, in CI): kill between hooks -> interrupted post hook with the pre hook's token; unfinished first; daemon catch-up for backup + maintenance; shutdown vs asked-for stop; a stopped first backup logs `Incomplete snapshot saved` and the next `Previous incomplete backup contains`; drill leftovers deleted, a recorded service path refused. sigterm-stop.sh now also proves `docker stop` keeps the run and `docker start` reruns and finishes it. Ran locally: both + fault-kill, hook-failures, lock-concurrency, maintenance, pause-resume, restore-drill, stop-go, stop-nonfinal, stop-skips-prune; unit tests -race; golangci-lint clean.

Codex: 9 rounds. Taken partly: a record that cannot be written before a pre hook warns rather than skipping the service (a missed backup is worse than the double fault). Conflicts expected with #215 in worker.go (its hold() should also terminate in the background).

body:
The Duplicacy half of ADR 46: `build/duplicacy/resume-point.patch`, applied in the Dockerfile after the Dropbox patch, with its test run during the build.

- `EntryList.SaveResumePoint`: saves where a backup is without ending it. `incomplete_snapshot` (the entries, unchanged during the upload) is written once per backup and `incomplete_chunks` is replaced atomically each time; files and the directory are fsynced. It holds the upload-completion lock and is called from the packing goroutine (`uploadChunkFunc`) every `DUPLICACY_RESUME_INTERVAL` seconds (default 300; 0 = every chunk, negative = never). A crash at any instant leaves the previous point or this one; a pair from two backups fails the token check.
- Incremental (quick mode) backups now load an incomplete snapshot too, and `RunAtError` saves for every non-dry-run backup (was hash mode only).
- Before using an incomplete snapshot, every chunk it names that the cache does not already hold (the previous revision's, or the whole listing on a fast-listing first backup) is looked up on the storage; one missing discards it (`INCOMPLETE_DISCARD`). Covers an exhaustive prune deleting an interrupted backup's chunks once its snapshot ID counts as inactive (7 days), and preserved chunks from a first interruption after a second.
- A packed file's size and hash are written under the same lock, so the SIGINT save never sees one without the other.

Tests: `TestResumePoint` (first/incremental x in-memory/on-disk, a pruned uploaded chunk, interrupted twice with a first-attempt chunk pruned): stops a backup just after a resume point, checks the files finished then are not read again and every file restores byte for byte; -race clean; each fix has a negative run that fails without it. Upstream TestBackupManager/TestEntryList/TestPersistRestore pass. fault-interrupt.sh gains a SIGKILLed incremental backup (no signal handled) that resumes from its periodic save and restores byte for byte. Cross-version e2e suite passed on the final image (634 s).

Codex: diff reviews clean after fixes; a cold `cx verify` of the never-wrong-revision claim found the prune and torn-save holes (fixed). Rejected: a file rewritten with the same size and mtime keeps its old content on resume; that is quick mode's own trust model, and upstream's hash-mode resume already has it.

Upstream: to be offered to gilbertchen/duplicacy in teaching mode, with Cody, only when he approves.

The V1 security follow-up from the early audit. Duplicacy 3.2.5 wrote a snapshot's files through an existing link to a directory (and into a link to a file when restoring in place), so whoever could write the destination chose where restored files landed; #186 only warned.

`build/duplicacy/restore-links.patch` (applied after resume-point.patch; its test runs in the image build):
- A link where the snapshot has a directory or a file: replaced with it when overwriting, the restore stops otherwise (RESTORE_LINKDIR / RESTORE_LINKFILE).
- Nothing (file, directory, link) is created, replaced or removed below a link to a directory that the restore does not replace (a partial restore): fails that entry (counted with allowFailures, else the restore stops).
- `-delete` does not delete the directory that replaced a link (a relative or nested link lists as `d`, the directory as `d/`).
- Quick mode skips a file as unchanged only when a regular file is really there (the listing follows top-level links, so a linked file looks unchanged).

TestRestoreNeverFollowsLinks covers refusal, replacement, partial restores below a linked parent (file, directory, link, nested file), -delete over relative and nested links, and quick mode over a linked file and a linked directory; nothing a link points to may change. Negative runs: the unpatched restore writes through both links; removing the deletion skip or the quick-mode guard each fails the test. (One quick-mode directory case Codex raised did not reproduce; its guard stays, exercised by the linked-file case.) Upstream TestBackupManager, TestPersistRestore, TestResumePoint pass.

Archiver: the pre-restore warning now says what happens; restore-commands.sh adds a linked file refused without OVERWRITE and replaced with it, the target untouched. restore-drill, recover, roundtrip pass; e2e passed.

Codex: 5 rounds (partial restores below a linked parent, -delete, quick mode found and fixed).

Upstream: to be offered in teaching mode with Cody only when he approves.

Every Duplicacy repository (service, copy, maintenance, restore, drill, probe) links its known_hosts to one owner-only record under logs/.ssh, so a key seen once is checked by all of them and survives container recreation; the recovery kit's OpenSSH known_hosts moves there too.

- Container start seeds the record from every existing pin (service repositories, the old in-tree .duplicacy of each service directory, copy and maintenance repositories, the kit's $HOME/.ssh copy), reading only files Archiver owns that nobody else can write.
- A repository pinning a different key for a server the record knows is refused, left in place, and named.
- build/duplicacy/host-keys-append.patch opens known_hosts with O_APPEND, so concurrent processes never overwrite each other's keys (TestHostKeysAppendConcurrently fails 3/3 without it).
- sftp-runtime.sh: after the server's keys change, backup and restore are refused.

Not done: locking Duplicacy's whole check-and-append. Two processes making the very first contact with one server at the same instant can still each trust what answers; that is trust on first use either way.

Two commits.

1. Each patch in build/duplicacy/ opens with what it changes, why, the test that proves it and its upstream status; build/duplicacy/series lists the order. The Dockerfile applies the series (patches touching vendor/ after go mod vendor), collects the tests from the patches' `Test: TestX` lines and requires every one to pass. The old Dockerfile comment (which had missed gcd-drive-id) shrinks to a pointer.
2. dependencies.patch: Duplicacy's golang.org/x/crypto v0.12.0 -> v0.58.0, x/net v0.10.0 -> v0.61.0, x/text, x/oauth2 to latest (Go 1.19 -> 1.26 language version; grpc stays v1.28.1, pinned by Google's cloud libraries). Patch tests run with -vet=off (Go 1.26 vet rejects upstream format strings). Duplicacy's TestPersistRestore needs GODEBUG=randseednop=0 under Go 1.24+ and is not run by the build; with it the upstream suite matches the unpatched baseline.

Verified locally on the image: the 5 patch tests; sftp-runtime; every backends.sh type; all 43 round-trip scripts; the e2e cross-version suite; arm64: the official 3.2.5 arm64 binary and ours restore each other's erasure-coded backups byte-identical with check -chunks clean. The first commit alone builds and passes its tests.

body:
Cody's decisions of 2026-10-12/13 for folding the NAS archiver-drill container into Archiver, text approved verbatim (including two later revisions: ADR 50 resets verified-chunk progress after a completed check; ADR 51 covers OneDrive, whose envelope cannot hold a token):

- 48 a per-service drill hook proves a restored service is usable
- 49 a drill checks every restored file against the revision's record (supersedes ADR 28's file-count check)
- 50 a scheduled deep check reads every chunk of a storage
- 51 a kit drill rehearses recovery from the envelope alone
- 52 per-kind schedules (due until it passes, time limits), one metric naming on METRICS_PORT, drill notifications on by default with a NOTIFY_ON opt-out
head: refs/pull/238/head
title: docs(adr): 48-52, the drill gate

body:
- After a drill restores a revision, every entry the revision records (duplicacy cat) must be in the copy with its type, size, mtime and mode (a link's target); nothing extra but duplicacy's top-level .duplicacy. Duplicacy has already verified content hashes. Replaces the file count (ADR 49).
- Then the service's executable `drill` hook (service dir or HOOKS_DIR, ADR 45 rules) runs in the restored copy with RestoreEnviron + ARCHIVER_DRILL_DIR; exit 0 passes; RESTORE_DRILL_HOOK_TIMEOUT (default 6h, paused time not counted); its whole process group is ended on exit, stop or timeout (ADR 48).
- doctor checks a drill hook like the others; backups warn about restore/drill hooks left in a service dir under HOOKS_DIR.

Tests: verify_test.go, drill_hook_test.go (pass/fail/timeout/unsafe/env/cwd/child cleanup/pause), restore-drill.sh cases for a passing and a failing hook; lint, race tests; restore-drill.sh, restore-commands.sh, hook-safety.sh on a local image. Depends on the ADR PR #238 for the ADR files.
head: refs/pull/239/head
title: feat(drill): check restored entries against the revision's record, and run the service's drill hook (ADRs 48, 49)

body:
Two commits.

1. fix(maintenance): maintenance run without the copy workers pruned secondary storages directly, ignoring the in-use registry, so a restore or drill reading a secondary could lose its revision. It now takes deletions from a dry run and skips revisions in use, reusing the primary's filtered prune.
2. feat(deep-check): STORAGE_TARGET_N_DEEP_CHECK (cron, unset = off) and `archiver deep-check [STORAGE]` run `check -chunks` from a repository of its own on the logs volume. verified_chunks is kept across an interruption and cleared once a check completes (Duplicacy otherwise skips chunks it verified before). A starting backup interrupts it (SIGINT, progress saved) and it stays due; DEEP_CHECK_TIMEOUT (default 7d); stop and pause act on it; shutdown waits for it to save progress; the revision hold and run lock pass to the duplicacy child. Damage raises an incident naming the chunks (zero-length ones included); a pass clears it. Metrics per storage: archiver_deep_check_last_timestamp_seconds, _last_ok, _last_duration_seconds, _last_success_timestamp_seconds; status shows the last check.

Tests: unit tests for config, progress clearing, metrics, incidents, shutdown, the child-held locks; tests/integration/deep-check.sh (clean pass, a corrupted and a zero-length chunk named, resume vs clear) added to CI; maintenance, restore-drill, prune-in-use and copy-workers scripts rerun. Lint and race tests clean. Three Codex review rounds; findings fixed.
head: refs/pull/240/head
title: feat(deep-check): scheduled deep storage checks (ADR 50), and standalone maintenance honours in-use revisions on secondaries

body:
KIT_DRILL_SCHEDULE (cron, unset = off) and `archiver kit-drill [STORAGE]`: for each offsite storage, fetch the recovery kit with only the credentials the envelope prints (break-glass, else the backup credential the envelope falls back to; SFTP with the break-glass key; OneDrive with Archiver's own token, status noting the sign-in step is left to a person), decrypt with stock openssl (password off argv) in a private scratch dir, and require every expected entry, the same content as the local kit and current secrets. Due until it passes, KIT_DRILL_TIMEOUT (6h), stop/pause; termination cancels and removes decrypted scratch, stale scratch from a killed drill is removed at start; initialization failures raise a run-level incident. Incidents per storage, archiver_kit_drill_* metrics, status.

Tests: unit tests (credential scope, OneDrive fallback, expected entries, secret comparison, cancellation cleanup, init incidents, metrics); tests/integration/kit-drill.sh (host-driven: Garage stand-in + atmoz/sftp; pass, stale kit, revoked S3 and SFTP credentials, recovery) in CI; sftp-runtime, recovery-kit, invalid-cron, deep-check rerun. Two Codex review rounds; findings fixed.
head: refs/pull/241/head
title: feat(kit-drill): rehearse recovery from the envelope alone (ADR 51)

body:
- Restore drills, deep checks and kit drills stay due after a failure or an interruption (stop, timeout) and run again at the next scheduled time until one passes; genuine skips (no revision yet, too little space) still let rotation advance.
- RESTORE_DRILL_TIMEOUT ends a restore drill like a stop.
- Metrics: archiver_restore_drill_last_timestamp_seconds, _last_ok, _last_duration_seconds, _last_success_timestamp_seconds per storage and service, matching archiver_deep_check_* and archiver_kit_drill_*; archiver_drill_last_ok and archiver_drill_last_timestamp_seconds kept as deprecated aliases.
- NOTIFY_ON=failures,-drills (also per destination) leaves drill results out of notifications; incidents, status, health and metrics still record them. Default unchanged: drill failures notify.

Tests: unit tests for each (pending vs skip vs interruption, timeout, metric names and aliases, opt-out suppression and re-eligibility of undelivered alerts, failure incident raised even when the state write fails); restore-drill.sh, metrics.sh, incidents.sh, deep-check.sh, kit-drill.sh rerun. Three Codex review rounds; findings fixed.
head: refs/pull/242/head
title: feat(drill): due until it passes, time limits, one metric naming, and a NOTIFY_ON opt-out for drill results (ADR 52)

body:
Two commits: ADR 53 (text approved by Cody), and its implementation.

RESTORE_DRILL_<NAME>_SCHEDULE defines a named drill; _SERVICES (all of them each run), _STORAGES (all | primary | names | alternate | alternate:NAME,NAME: one storage per run, in turn, cursor persisted, held on a storage until a run there passes), _TIMEOUT. Each named drill is its own kind under ADR 52 (due until it passes, time limit), with its own state, incidents, status lines (also on the HTML status page, with deep-check and kit-drill results) and metrics: archiver_restore_drill_* gains a drill label (default or the name; new series identities), archiver_drill_* aliases unchanged. NOTIFY_ON -drills covers them. Drill hooks run as usual. Use case: a whole object store drilled monthly from offsite storages in turn, excluded from the regular rotation.

Tests: config parsing/validation (name rule vs existing keys), alternate and alternate:LIST rotation through failures/restarts/list changes, metrics labels, status and web rendering, opt-out; restore-drill.sh named case; metrics, incidents, invalid-cron, status page scripts. Two Codex review rounds; findings fixed.
head: refs/pull/243/head
title: feat(drill): named drill schedules (ADR 53)

body:
Found by the rc1 readiness review of the NAS upgrade.

- On/off environment settings (DRY_RUN, RUN_RESTORE_SERVICE, DELETE_EXTRA, HASH_COMPARE, OVERWRITE and the rest) were on for any non-empty value, so DRY_RUN=false meant a dry run. One shared parser: true/1/yes/on on, false/0/no/off/empty off, anything else refuses with a clear error. docs/upgrading.md lists the change.
- A drill hook that times out or is stopped now gets SIGTERM to its process group and RESTORE_DRILL_HOOK_GRACE (default 60s) to clean up (containers it started) before SIGKILL; pause cannot freeze that cleanup; a paused hook is resumed before SIGTERM. docs/hooks.md: trap TERM and clean up.

Tests for both (fail before, pass after); full race suite, lint, restore integration scripts, drill hook timeout/stop cleanup. Two Codex review rounds. Committed together because they share the config, docs and CHANGELOG hunks.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>moby/moby</summary>

### [`v29.9.1`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.9.1): v29.9.1

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.9.0-rc.2...docker-v29.9.1)

##### 29.9.1

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.9.1 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.1)
- [moby/moby, 29.9.1 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.1)

##### Security

The containerd update to v2.4.2 includes fixes for the following security vulnerabilities:

- [CVE-2026-95839](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-vwhp-8p66-mq4f): Pulling or importing an image through containerd's transfer service could crash containerd if a child descriptor contained the `io.containerd.manifest.subject` annotation and a malformed digest.
- [GHSA-8647-2jxj-p2rc](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-8647-2jxj-p2rc): An untrusted registry returning a crafted `Content-Length` header could crash containerd when parallel layer fetching was enabled with `concurrent_layer_fetch_buffer`.
- [GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-hc94-p972-ch66): Pulling a crafted image or pulling from a malicious registry could exhaust host disk space because containerd did not limit incoming layer data to the declared size before validation.

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Fix `--link-local-ip` accepting addresses that are not link-local (169.254.0.0/16 or fe80::/10) when creating a container or connecting it to a network, which  made the container fail to start. [moby/moby#53923](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53923)
- Fix `COPY --from` in the classic builder failing for files not owned by root when userns-remap is enabled. [moby/moby#53859](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53859)
- Fix `docker ps -s` and container listing with sizes failing entirely when the size of one container cannot be computed. [moby/moby#53921](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53921)
- Fix `docker save` leaving image layers on disk after the image is removed, when the image contains the same layer more than once (graph-driver image store). [moby/moby#53927](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53927)
- Fix a daemon panic when using the `fluentd` log driver with a TLS address that cannot be connected to and `fluentd-async` enabled. [moby/moby#53922](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53922)
- Fix image digest resolution failing when a registry mirror succeeds but a subsequent registry lookup fails. [moby/moby#53933](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53933)
- Fix plugin privilege lookup reporting success when fetching the plugin fails. [moby/moby#53934](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53934)

##### Packaging updates

- Update containerd (static binaries) to [v2.4.2](https://github.com/containerd/containerd/releases/tag/v2.4.2). [moby/moby#53936](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53936)

##### Networking

- Don't add bridge network interfaces to firewalld's `docker` zone when `iptables` and `ip6tables` are both disabled. [moby/moby#53907](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53907)
- Fix bridge networks failing to restore on daemon startup when their bridge is bound to a firewalld zone other than `docker`. [moby/moby#53907](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53907)

##### Rootless

- Fix `--domainname` with user namespaces and rootless mode; this requires an OCI runtime supporting the `domainname` field (such as runc >= v1.2.0). [moby/moby#53899](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53899)
- Update RootlessKit to [v3.3.0](https://github.com/rootless-containers/rootlesskit/releases/tag/v3.3.0). [moby/moby#53942](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53942)

</details>

body:
A restore into a service directory holds the restore lock, which keeps backups out. Its post-restore hook died with Archiver (Pdeathsig), but what the hook ran in the foreground (a shell's long command) ran on, writing to the service directory with the lock already released.

- The hook now runs under a hidden `archiver hook-guard`: the guard inherits the restore lock (fd 3, never passed on to the hook), runs the hook in its own process group, and if the restore dies kills that group and holds the lock until none of it runs. A daemon the hook starts in its own session is left alone, as before.
- The hook gets the terminal (/dev/tty) while it runs, also when the restore's answers are piped; Ctrl-Z stops the whole restore job and fg resumes the hook.
- Tests: tests/integration/restore-commands.sh case (fails on main: the lock was free while the hook's child still wrote), internal/hooks/guard_test.go (lock held until the foreground is gone, daemon survives, lock not inherited, PTY with piped stdin, Ctrl-Z continue). Job control also checked by hand with an interactive bash: jobs showed Stopped, fg resumed the hook.
- A hook killed by a signal now reports 128+signal (was -1).
