title: fix(restore): a killed restore keeps the restore lock until its hook's foreground processes are gone

body:
Item: the known flakes TestRunsPauseResume and TestRunsRefusedBackupNotifies.

Evidence (Forgejo Actions logs, all black-box failures since 2026-09-29):
- TestRunsRefusedBackupNotifies failed on main once (2026-10-07, task 104176): a single TLS handshake timeout to the fake notifier lost the alert. Fixed that night by 0ea32e9 (transient notification failures are retried). Its earlier stall (2026-10-04, task 97523) was on release/0.11 (bash).
- TestRunsPauseResume failed only on v0.11.4 (bash, task 97766); the bash pause gap was fixed in 0.11.6.
- Neither has failed on main since; the other black-box failures were image-build or network errors.

Residual race fixed here: archiver pause recorded the pause, signalled, slept 300 ms and signalled again to catch a program the pipeline started between its pause check and the start. A busy host can outrun 300 ms, leaving that program running while the backup reports paused. Now the pause (runlock.Pause, as the drill already uses) and every program start (duplicacy and hooks, runlock.(*Lock).Unpaused) hold the lock-file edit lock: a start either finishes first and is stopped, or sees the pause and waits. A pre-backup hook held back by a pause and then stopped does not start (Codex review); post-backup hooks still do.

Tests: TestUnpausedExcludesPause, TestStopDuringPauseSkipsOnlyThePreHook (fails without the skip); go test -race ./cmd/... ./internal/...; golangci-lint 0 issues; e2e on the bench daemon: the two tests 20x each (40/40) and, after the review fix, all TestRuns* 3x plus the two 10x each (68/68).

Regression tests for two faults noted open after the copy-workers merge (#133). Both are fixed on main; this proves it and keeps them fixed. Test-only.

**A newly registered secondary could fail maintenance once.** At 6f9c29f, bash maintenance ran from a service repository that did not know a secondary a copy worker had just registered, so its check and prune of that secondary failed. Go maintenance now registers each secondary in its own repository (`internal/maintenance/repo.go` `addSecondary`, from df250e8) and keeps to local while workers run.

**First-time registration contacted the target from the backup, waiting on it.** 7e9167b (#175) made `addStorages` return early under copy workers, but removed the only tests and added none.

New coverage:
- `copy-workers.sh`: restart the daemon with a new local secondary `fourth` and wait for its worker to catch it up. Then:
  - maintenance must pass;
  - after a backup, the service repository's preferences must name `local` but not `fourth`;
  - the worker must copy the new revision to `fourth`.
- `maintenance.sh`: without a daemon, a never-created secondary is created, checked and pruned by the first maintenance, with no error.

Proof the new block catches the faults:
- On an image built at 7e9167b^ it fails: the backup registered `fourth`.
- On an image built at 6f9c29f it fails: `Storage check failed for fourth`.
- On main efc295f it passes.

Both full scripts pass on the bench.

body:
On a Synology share mounted into the container, an ACL file shows a mode that depends on its owner: the freshly placed kit stats 0 while root-owned and 0700 after the chown to config's owner. `adjust()` compared the pre-chown stat with config's 0700, chmod'ed, and any chmod on synoacl converts the file to plain Linux mode, dropping the inherited ACL that grants the mirror user read. The readability check passed because config also reads 0700 inside the container.

- re-stat after the chown
- when config carries a Synology ACL (`system.syno_acl_inherit`/`_self` xattr), never chmod, and require the kit to carry one too (else Unverified, re-placed next run)
- stateVersion 5 -> 6 so existing deployments re-place once

Proven on the NAS in a scratch share with the rc.1 image and caps: rclone copyto, rename and chown keep the ACL; chown + chmod reproduces the 0700 Linux-mode kit; a probe of the new logic detects the ACL through /proc/self/fd and flags a stripped file. Unit tests, go vet and gofmt pass.

A kit upload that failed (cowanserver timed out at 04:01 on 2026-10-19) or was skipped because the storage was down waited for the next backup, up to a day, with the Recovery Kit Failed incident open, although the message already promised "placed when it is back".

- Backups and manual `recovery-kit` now take the same lock, so two placements never interleave.
- The kit no longer says up to date on all storage targets when it skipped a down storage.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>moby/moby</summary>

### [`v29.9.2`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.9.2): v29.9.2

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.9.1...docker-v29.9.2)

##### 29.9.2

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.9.2 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.2)
- [moby/moby, 29.9.2 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.9.2)

##### Security

The Go runtime update addresses [CVE-2026-111943](https://go.dev/issue/82345) by rejecting certificate chains that include eight revoked eMudhra intermediate certificates.
Image pulls and pushes fail TLS certificate verification if a registry's certificate chain relies on one of the affected TLS intermediates.
Affected registries need a replacement certificate chain that does not use these intermediates.

The blocked intermediates are:

- Domain-validated TLS: `EM DV TLS CA - G3B` and `EM DV TLS CA - G3C`
- Organization-validated TLS: `EM OV TLS CA - G3B` and `EM OV TLS CA - G3C`
- Extended-validation TLS: `EM EV TLS CA - G3B` and `EM EV TLS CA - G3C`
- Code signing: `EM OV CS CA - G3B` and `EM OV CS CA - G3C`

The G3B intermediates belong to eMudhra BV, and the G3C intermediates belong to eMudhra Inc.
The keys for these intermediates were compromised.

##### Packaging updates

- Update Go runtime to [1.26.10](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.26.10). [moby/moby#53989](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53989), [docker/cli#7418](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7418)

GARAGE drill run 5 failed 22h and ~98% into its B2 restore on one `connection reset by peer`: Duplicacy 3.2.5 retries a chunk download only on io.ErrUnexpectedEOF. New patch `build/duplicacy/download-retry-network.patch` retries reset/aborted/broken-pipe/timeout up to 8 times with a 2s doubling backoff capped at 1m.

Test-first: `TestChunkDownloadRetriesNetworkErrors` drives a real download through a storage that cuts off N times; it fails on the image without the retry hunk (reset and timeout not retried) and passes with it. A non-network error is still not retried; a link that never comes back gives up after 9 downloads. Codex review: no findings.

body: config:recommended includes :ignoreModulesAndTests, whose ignorePaths has **/tests/**, so includePaths entries tests/e2e/Dockerfile, tests/fakes/Dockerfile and tests/integration/podman.sh were never updated. Their golang pin sat at 1.27.2 while the build image moved to 1.27.3, and #270 (go 1.27.3 in go.mod) failed the e2e build. Overrides ignorePaths with the preset minus the test globs and brings both test golang pins to the build image digest. renovate-config-validator --strict passes on Renovate 44.151.2.
head: refs/pull/276/head
title: fix(renovate): track the Dockerfiles and scripts under tests/

body: The aliases were kept for one release (rc1) after the restore drill metrics moved to archiver_restore_drill_* with a drill label. No alert rule or dashboard in the deployment repos reads them. Unit and integration tests now assert they are gone; docs and CHANGELOG updated.
head: refs/pull/277/head
title: chore(metrics): drop the archiver_drill_* restore drill aliases

body: Under pipefail, `cmd | grep -q PATTERN` can fail although PATTERN is present: grep exits at its first match and the writer takes SIGPIPE. restore-drill.sh:142 failed the Round-trip job on #264 this way. Every piped grep -q in tests/ (36) becomes `grep PATTERN >/dev/null`, and tests/lint/piped-grep-q.sh runs as a CI job gating the build jobs so the pattern cannot come back.

body: Found by the vps kit-only recovery drill (2026-10-29): `archiver recover` created each service directory as root, while vps needs /srv dirs owned by uid 1000. A Duplicacy snapshot holds a directory's contents, not the directory, so the kit now records each existing service directory's uid, gid and mode (with setuid/setgid/sticky) in services.json, and recover applies them when it creates the directory, before the restore and its hook. Honors DRY_RUN and IGNORE_OWNERSHIP; without CHOWN+FOWNER it sets only the mode, like the restore. Warns when the kernel drops setgid (no CAP_FSETID). Adding the file re-uploads each kit once; older kits recover as before.
head: refs/pull/301/head
title: fix(recover): recreate service directories with their recorded owner and mode

body:
Nothing ever removed the snapshots of a service taken out of SERVICE_DIRECTORIES: Duplicacy's prune never deletes an ID's newest revision and passes over an ID with no revision in 7 days, and mirroring leaves alone an ID the primary lacks. The NAS kept 13 such IDs (forgejo 61 GB on B2).

- `archiver forget NAME... [--yes]` lists what each storage holds, asks, then deletes `snapshots/<id>/` via the kit's rclone remote, primary first, under each storage's in-use gate (re-listing there, skipping an ID a copy or restore reads). Refuses configured services (unmounted literal dirs included), invalid IDs, and deletes nothing unless every storage lists. Chunks go in the next exhaustive prune (two-step, safe beside backups).
- `archiver doctor` warns about this host's IDs no configured service backs up.
- `config.ServiceName` resolves a service dir like the pipeline does (doctor named `.` wrong).
- tests: unit (internal/forget, doctor), integration `tests/integration/forget.sh` in CI.

body:
The NAS envelope (local, B2 break-glass, SFTP full access + ed25519 key) is 2 pages on rc4: its last paragraph's second line spills. When a layout runs over, the PDF is laid out again with vertical spacing at 95/90/85% and the first one-page result is kept; font sizes and QR codes unchanged, a page needing more keeps full spacing. Only the PDF renderer changes: Page elements and the fingerprint do not, so a confirmed envelope stays confirmed.

Verified: a 5-storage envelope is /Count 2 on rc4 and /Count 1 with this build; unit test TestEnvelopeFitsOneSheetWhenItCan.

body:
A backup that finished while a copy worker was mirroring, exhaustively pruning, copying or held by its copy window left the target's behind count (status, backup health, `archiver_copy_behind_revisions`) at its pre-backup value until that work ended. On the NAS, cowanserver read 0 behind while really 9 behind during a 7h mirror prune, so a copy-lag alert could not fire.

- A wake now recounts from a listing of the primary only (the target is not touched): still-missing revisions from the last listing plus everything local gained since.
- A listing that finds the target caught up clears the count; a pass that catches up does not zero a count a backup raised mid-pass.
- New gauge `archiver_copy_busy_since_timestamp_seconds{target,activity}` for alerting on a prune or copy that runs too long.
- Status lines show "N revisions behind" while busy.

Tests: TestBackupDuringPruneRaisesBehind (fails on main), TestCopyThenUpkeepNotBehind, TestIdleWakeLeavesCountToPass; full unit suite with -race; copier package 20x stable.

body:
On 11/1 the NAS redeployed archiver for rc.4 while the monthly local deep check was 71% through its 441k chunks. The check stopped with its verified chunks saved and its run record kept, but nothing read that record back: ADR 46 catch-up covered backups, maintenance, drills and kit drills, not deep checks. So it stayed failed and due until 12/1, and `ArchiverDeepCheckFailed` would have fired for a month.

- On start, interrupted deep checks run again (daemon and no-schedule modes) and resume from their verified chunks.
- Like maintenance and drills, only a container shutdown (or a crash) keeps the record. A pass, a damage failure, a manual stop, a timeout or giving way to a backup ends it and keeps the documented retry at the next slot. A failed check no longer reruns its full read at every restart.
- The record now carries the configured storage name, so names that `config.Sanitize` changes (`local-backups`) map back to their schedule and command. A record for a storage since removed is dropped instead of retried forever.
- Fixed in passing: in no-schedule mode an interrupted named drill ran `archiver drill:<name>`, which is not a command. Both catch-up paths now share `catchUpArgs`.

Tests: shutdown keeps the record and every other end clears it (`TestProgressAndIncidents`); catch-up names match `daemon.Jobs` and map to runnable commands, sanitized names included; a removed storage drops its record. `go vet ./...` and `go test -race ./cmd/... ./internal/...` pass. The new catch-up test fails with the fix removed.

Maintenance keeps to local while copy workers check and mirror the secondaries (ADRs 12, 17, 18), so status, the web page and `archiver_storage_last_{check,prune}_timestamp_seconds` kept showing each secondary's last maintenance run from before the workers took over: on the NAS, cowanserver and backblaze read as unpruned since 10/14 although both mirror daily.

A secondary now takes the later of maintenance's record and its worker's last check, mirror pass (as its prune) and exhaustive prune. healthcheck already skipped worker-kept secondaries and is unchanged.

Test: TestSecondaryMaintenanceFromWorker. Full unit suite with -race; Codex review clean.

body:
ADR 54. A kit drill that has never run waited for its first slot, so a monthly schedule could leave the envelope path unproven for weeks.

With KIT_DRILL_SCHEDULE set, the daemon now starts one when an offsite storage has no drill on record and every offsite storage holds the current kit. It checks at container start and after each successful scheduled backup, on its own goroutine so a stalled or paused drill never holds up a backup. Restore drills and deep checks keep their first slots.

The kit carries the settings, the schedule among them, so setting the schedule makes the placed kit stale: tests/integration/kit-drill.sh covers that case, the first drill at start, and no repeat once every storage is drilled.

body:
Kit, restore and named drills share one lock. A scheduled drill whose time came while another ran was refused, with no notification, and left for its next slot: a month for a monthly drill.

The daemon now has the drills it starts take turns: the second waits and starts when the first ends, and also waits for a drill started by hand. `archiver stop` drops a waiting drill along with the running one; a drill still waiting when the container stops runs at its next scheduled time. The first kit drill (ADR 54) never waits.

Proof: the new phases in tests/integration/restore-drill.sh fail on main with "A restore drill is already running" and pass here, including the stop phase.

title: fix(drills): scheduled drills whose times meet take turns

body: The Podman 6 image sets journald as the log driver in a vendor drop-in that wins over its own containers.conf, and the test host runs no journal, so `podman logs` stayed empty and the readiness wait timed out. Archiver itself runs under Podman 6.1.3. With `--log-driver k8s-file` the test passes on 5.8.9 and 6.1.3, which unblocks #328.

title: test(podman): name the log driver

body:
Since #334 a scheduled drill waits for the running one, but only the daemon log said so. `archiver status` now prints `Drills waiting their turn: ...` and `status --json` carries `drills_waiting`. The daemon keeps the list in the lock directory, written atomically and cleared at its start.

tests/integration/restore-drill.sh checks status while a drill waits and after a stop.
head: refs/pull/336/head
title: feat(status): status lists the scheduled drills waiting their turn

body:
On the NAS, RECOVERY_KIT_EXTRA_PATHS holds files that change daily (DSM config, git bundles), so `archiver doctor` warned that the kit was not yet placed for most of every day.

The kit now also records a core fingerprint (the same hash without extra/) in logs/.recovery-kit-core. Doctor says OK, naming the storages, when a storage holds a kit whose core is current and only extras changed; it still warns when settings, keys or notes changed. The full fingerprint and its state file are unchanged, so no kit is re-uploaded. Storages a refresh leaves alone keep their place on the core record, and a run with nothing to upload still writes it.

Tests: new phase in tests/integration/doctor.sh (fails on main), unit tests for both review findings.

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [moby/moby](https://github.com/moby/moby) | minor | `29.9.3` → `29.10.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>moby/moby</summary>

### [`v29.10.0`](https://github.com/moby/moby/releases/tag/docker-v29.10.0): v29.10.0

[Compare Source](https://github.com/moby/moby/compare/docker-v29.9.3...docker-v29.10.0-rc.2)

##### 29.10.0

For a full list of pull requests and changes in this release, refer to the relevant GitHub milestones:

- [docker/cli, 29.10.0 milestone](https://github.com/docker/cli/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.10.0)
- [moby/moby, 29.10.0 milestone](https://github.com/moby/moby/issues?q=is%3Aclosed+milestone%3A29.10.0)

##### ⚠️ Potential breaking change: local registry connections

If you explicitly configure `insecure-registries` in `daemon.json` or use `--insecure-registry`, Docker Engine no longer automatically treats loopback addresses (`127.0.0.0/8` and `::1/128`) as insecure registries.

> \[!WARNING]
> After upgrading, pulls and pushes to local registries that use HTTP or untrusted TLS certificates may fail unless those registries are explicitly included in your insecure registry configuration.
> Configure TLS with a trusted certificate, or add only the required local registry addresses, such as `localhost:5000`, to your existing insecure registry configuration.

When `insecure-registries` is omitted, loopback registries remain insecure by default.
Setting `"insecure-registries": []` in `daemon.json` disables all default insecure registries. [moby/moby#53868](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53868)

##### 🧻 Engine API specification moves to OpenAPI 3.2

The Engine API specification now uses OpenAPI 3.2 as its source format, in [`api/openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/api/v1.57.0/api/openapi.yaml).
A Swagger 2.0 specification generated from it is still published for existing tooling, in [`api/swagger.yaml`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/api/v1.57.0/api/swagger.yaml).
For the transition, this release also includes a Swagger 2.0 copy pinned to API v1.57, in [`api/docs/v1.57-swagger.yaml`](https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/api/v1.57.0/api/docs/v1.57-swagger.yaml).
Future API versions won't get a per-version Swagger 2.0 copy, so update tooling that depends on these files to use the OpenAPI 3.2 specifications. [moby/moby#53630](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53630)

##### 📦 Packages for AlmaLinux, Oracle Linux, and Rocky Linux

Docker Engine packages are available for AlmaLinux, Oracle Linux, and Rocky Linux.
For installation instructions, see [AlmaLinux](/manuals/engine/install/almalinux.md), [Oracle Linux](/manuals/engine/install/oraclelinux.md), and [Rocky Linux](/manuals/engine/install/rockylinux.md).

***

##### New

- Add experimental support for jobs: run one-shot and cron-scheduled workloads natively managed by the daemon, as an opt-in built-in extension enabled with `--enable-extension org.mobyproject.jobs.v0`. [moby/moby#53485](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53485)
- Add support for customizing Docker’s embedded containerd using configuration files in `/etc/docker/containerd.d/`. [moby/moby#53946](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53946)
- Introduce `restarting` attribute for  `die` events to let consumer know container is going to restart. [moby/moby#50908](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/50908)

##### Bug fixes and enhancements

- Block obsolete socket families in the default AppArmor and seccomp profiles. [moby/moby#54093](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54093)
- containerd image store: Fix `docker image inspect` and `docker image ls` reporting an empty image when the host platform of a multi-platform image is not pulled but another platform is. [moby/moby#54040](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54040)
- Don't wait for the telemetry export timeout when the OTLP endpoint refuses connections. [docker/cli#7495](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7495)
- Fix `docker <unknown-command> --version` printing the CLI version instead of an "unknown command" error. [docker/cli#7408](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7408)
- Fix `docker cp` printing a "Successfully copied" message when the copy fails. [docker/cli#7515](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7515)
- Fix `docker manifest annotate` rejecting valid platforms not included in its predefined list of OS/architecture combinations, such as `linux/loong64`. [docker/cli#7448](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7448)
- Fix `docker ps` printing an empty `NAMES` column when all of a container's names contain a slash, such as when connected to a classic Swarm API. [docker/cli#7481](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7481)
- Fix the daemon deleting the docker0 interface on restart when it is configured with a user-managed bridge and default-address-pools. [moby/moby#54157](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54157)
- Fix Windows layer exports containing NTFS sparse files. [moby/moby#53745](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53745)
- Fix: Include HTTP status codes in JSON streaming errors to allow clients to correctly classify failures. [moby/moby#54133](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54133)
- Improve image selection on ARM64 Linux hosts to prefer the highest image variant supported by the host CPU. [moby/moby#53910](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53910)
- manifest annotate: add shell-completion for `--os` and `--arch`. [docker/cli#7449](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7449)
- Reject duplicate GPU counts consistently when shorthand and explicit count options are mixed. [docker/cli#7312](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7312)
- Stop automatically treating loopback registries as insecure when `insecure-registries` is explicitly configured, and allow disabling the default insecure registries by setting `"insecure-registries": []` in `daemon.json`. [moby/moby#53868](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53868)
- Update runc (in static binaries) to [v1.5.3](https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/releases/tag/v1.5.3). [moby/moby#54183](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54183)

##### Packaging updates

- Update BuildKit to [v0.35.0](https://github.com/moby/buildkit/releases/tag/v0.35.0). [moby/moby#54180](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54180)
- Update Go runtime to [1.27.4](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.27.4). [moby/moby#54176](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54176), [docker/cli#7506](https://github.com/docker/cli/pull/7506)

##### Networking

- Engines using the nftables firewall backend can now join a Swarm. (Experimental). [moby/moby#53125](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53125)
- Fix `docker network ls --filter type=builtin --filter type=custom` listing a random subset of networks. [moby/moby#54127](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54127)
- Fix a "rule exists" error when publishing more than one host port for the same container port with the nftables firewall backend and the userland proxy disabled. [moby/moby#54031](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54031)
- Fix a container starting with no networking after an earlier start failed with a network error, such as a published port already being in use. [moby/moby#52480](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/52480)
- Fix DNS resolution on user-defined networks when the host's /etc/resolv.conf is missing or contains no valid nameservers. [moby/moby#54140](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54140)
- Fix iptables rules and an empty `DOCKER` chain left behind when the daemon switches to the nftables firewall backend after a release older than 28.0.1 ran with iptables. [moby/moby#54129](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54129)
- Fix iptables rules not being restored after firewalld is stopped, or started after the daemon. [moby/moby#54012](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54012)
- Fix overlay network driver errors when a container gets the IP address of a container that was just removed on another node. [moby/moby#53833](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53833)
- Fix overlay networking failing to reconverge after a network partition when a Swarm manager has been replaced at a new address. [moby/moby#53715](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53715)
- Fix swarm services leaking a virtual IP address on their other networks each time allocation fails on one network, which could exhaust the subnets of those networks. [moby/moby#54148](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54148)
- Fix Swarm tasks failing to reach a service's published port via their own node's address when a host firewall, such as ufw, drops unsolicited incoming traffic. [moby/moby#54006](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54006)
- Fix the MTU of overlay network interfaces being 20 bytes too large when the Swarm data path is IPv6. [moby/moby#54067](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54067)
- Reduce nftables port-publishing overhead by batching firewall updates per endpoint and address family. [moby/moby#54011](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54011)
- Stop nodes in a Swarm cluster from exchanging full overlay network state with every manager once a minute when the cluster is healthy. [moby/moby#53715](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53715)

##### Rootless

- Allow the overlay2 storage driver in rootless mode when SELinux is enabled. [moby/moby#54048](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/54048)
- Fix `docker cp` failing with "remount-ro ... operation not permitted" in rootless mode on containers with a read-only bind mount from a `nosuid` or `nodev` filesystem. [moby/moby#53981](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53981)

##### API

- Update API version to 1.57. [moby/moby#53972](https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/53972)

</details>

body:
Forgejo treats an AGit pull request (pushed to `refs/for/main`, no fork needed) as untrusted and holds its runs for approval, but its payload reports this repository as the head (`head.repo.full_name == github.repository`), so the existing fork gate let it through. When a maintainer acts on an outsider's PR (reopen), Forgejo 17 runs this branch's workflows, with secrets, against the PR's commit (services/actions/trust.go). Outside contributors are about to be able to sign in with GitHub and open AGit PRs, so the gate now also requires `github.event.pull_request.flow == 0`.

Proof (throwaway SisyphusMD/agit-guard-proof-20261116): an AGit PR's payload has `flow=1` and head repo = base repo, and the gated job was skipped (run 37485); a branch PR has `flow=0` and the gated job ran (run 37486).

Outside PRs get CI when a maintainer, after reading the diff, pushes the head to a branch here.

This workflow had no gate: every PR job except shellcheck (reads files) and the CHANGELOG lint (awk) executed the PR's code. Those jobs are now gated; Renovate and own-branch PRs are unchanged.

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|
| [quay.io/podman/stable](https://quay.io/podman/stable) ([source](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman)) | minor | `v6.1.3` → `v6.2.0` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>podman-container-tools/podman (quay.io/podman/stable)</summary>

### [`v6.2.0`](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/releases/tag/v6.2.0)

[Compare Source](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/compare/v6.1.3...v6.2.0)

##### Security

- Addresses CVE-2026-121885, untrusted image labels could be used to trick podman auto-update into restarting incorrect systemd units [GHSA-55rm-rwr7-q2wr](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/security/advisories/GHSA-55rm-rwr7-q2wr).
- Addresses CVE-2026-111361, malicious containers images could be able to bypass Digest and Signature validation [GHSA-pggw-qqjf-6cxw](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/security/advisories/GHSA-pggw-qqjf-6cxw).
- Addresses CVE-2026-123876, default seccomp profile socket deny rule could be bypass by a malicious container.

##### Features

- The `podman push` command now supports a new option, `--platform`, which selects and pushes a single platform-specific manifest instead of the entire list.
- The `podman kube play` command now supports a new option, `--validate`, which determines how unrecognized YAML fields are handled ([#​18332](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/18332)).
- The `podman kube play` command now supports a new option, `--label`, to set labels on created containers, pods, volumes, and secrets ([#​26450](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/26450)).
- The `podman kube play` command can now create multiple pods if more than 1 replica is requested by a deployment using the new `--multiple-pods` option ([#​26769](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/26769)).
- The `podman kube play --build` command now supports building images from subdirectories of the main context directory ([#​28148](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28418)).
- Quadlet `.container` files now support a new key, `Umask`, to set the default umask for the created container ([#​25278](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25278)).
- All Quadlet files now support a new key, `SetMountsDependency`, configuring whether the generated unit will use `RequiresMountsFor`, `WantsMountsFor`, or no dependency at all on required source paths ([#​29946](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29946)).
- The `podman farm list` command now supports two new options, `--quiet`, which will print only the names of active farms, and `--noheading`, which omits column headers from the output.
- The `podman artifact ls` command now supports two new options, `--format=json`, which will output machine-readable JSON, and `--quiet`, which prints only artifact digests.
- The `podman create` command now supports a new option, `--passwd`, to add entries to `/etc/passwd` in the container (this has previously been available with `podman run`).
- The `podman info` command now includes detailed information on the features supported by OCI runtimes.
- The `podman events --filter` command now supports a new filter, `network=`, to filter to events pertaining to a specific network ([#​29387](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29387)).
- The `podman auto-update` command has been enabled on the remote Podman client.
- The `StartInterval` field in image healthcheck configuration is now respected, allowing images to configure startup healthchecks ([#​27724](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27724)).
- The `podman image scp` command now supports two new options, `--compression-format` and `--compression-level`, to compress data during transfer ([#​23192](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/23192)).
- The `podman auto-update` command now supports a new option, `--filter`, to selectively update only containers that match the given filters.
- The `podman ps --sort` command now allows sorting by pod.
- The `podman ps --filter` command now supports a new filter, `status!`, which matches containers not in the given state ([#​21398](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/21398)).

##### Changes

- Podman now requires Go v1.26 or higher to build.
- The Podman machine WSL provider now has native systemd support, existing machines continue to be supported for now with our old custom systemd setup. We require at least WSL version 2.5.1 now, although we recommend using at least 2.7.5 for proper nftables networking support.
- The `podman kube play` command now uses the `securityContext.seccompProfile` fields in Kubernetes YAML for Seccomp configuration. Support for the existing annotation-based configuration of Seccomp is now deprecated, and will be removed with Podman 7.0.
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now includes three new fields, `DNSNames` (containing all names the container can be accessed via), `IsInitCtr` (whether the container is an init container), and `InitContainerType` (what type of init container this is, if it is one) ([#​29811](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29811)).
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now only includes user-added DNS aliases in the `Aliases` field, which previously displayed all DNS aliases, improving Docker compatibility.
- The `podman inspect` command on containers now properly populates the `ConsoleSize` field for running containers ([#​28368](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28368)).
- Systemd units created by Podman healthchecks are now named much more clearly (`libpod-healthcheck-$CONTAINERID-$randsuffix.service`) ([#​29373](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29373)).
- Signal proxying is now enabled for attached `podman exec` commands. As such, killing a `podman exec` command with Control-C or similar should now also kill the processes started in the container (similar to how `podman run` already works) ([#​19486](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/19486)).
- The deprecated `--cpu-rt-period` and `--cpu-rt-runtime` options for `podman create`, `podman run`, `podman update`, and `podman container clone` are now hidden and undocumented. They have not been functional since the removal of cgroups v1 support and will be removed entirely in Podman v7.
- The `--health-startup-interval` option to `podman create`, `podman run`, and `podman update` has a new alias, `--health-start-interval`.
- When a startup healthcheck interval is specified, but no startup healthcheck command, the standard healthcheck command will be used instead.
- When using the `journald` event driver, timestamps are no longer included in logged events, as `journald` includes a timestamp already ([#​29835](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29835)).
- Quadlet can now create template instances from instance-specific drop-in directories without requiring an explicit instance file or symlink ([#​27636](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27636)).

##### Bugfixes

- Fixed a bug where passing an empty file to the `--ignorefile` option to `podman build` would cause the `.dockerignore` or `.containerignore` file in the context directory to be used, instead of not using an ignorefile at all ([#​25147](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25147)).
- Fixed a bug where the `Pod=` key in Quadlet `.container` files did not expand the `%N` specifier ([#​29108](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29108)).
- Fixed a bug where containers created with `--userns=auto` would report having a `private` user namespace in `podman inspect` after they started, but not when they were first created.
- Fixed a bug where logging was configured too late in the Podman init process to print errors from parsing configuration files ([#​25362](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25362)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman system prune --build` command could fail if a build container was removed while it was running.
- Fixed a bug where `copy` events from `podman machine cp` were not properly displayed by the remote Podman client.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman farm build --tag` command would fail if given a tag including a colon ([#​25039](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25039)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine init --image` command would fail when given a read-only disk image.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine start` and `podman machine init --now` commands could hang on Windows systems using the Hyper-V provider if the VM failed to start ([#​29455](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29455)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine start` command on Windows (both Hyper-V and WSL providers) would sometimes fail due to leftover processes from previous machines ([#​29474](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29474)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine start` command could hang indefinitely if the VM failed to start properly ([#​29880](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29880)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine start` command could create a VM that cannot be connected to on Windows if the host was shut down or restarted when the VM was running ([#​29971](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29971)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine init` command on Windows when using the Hyper-V provider did not correctly detach the file server process, causing VMs to lose access to host shares when the console that ran `podman machine init` closed ([#​29573](http://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29573)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman kube play` command incorrectly handled `emptyDir` volumes with `medium: Memory`, causing them to not be shared between containers in the pod and to ignore the `sizeLimit` parameter ([#​29555](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29555)).
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman kube play` command incorrectly handled authentication credentials in API requests.
- Fixed a bug where volumes created by the `podman volume import` command would not adjust their permissions on being mounted into a container ([#​25442](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25442)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman build` command could leak temporary directories if a build failed ([#​22642](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/22642)).
- Fixed a bug where containers created with `--userns=keep-id` would use an image-specified user instead of forcing the same UID/GID in use on the host ([#​29600](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29600)).
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client could not function when connecting over SSH to a server which does not support the direct-streamlocal channel type ([#​27814](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27814)).
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman push`, `podman artifact push`, and `podman manifest push` commands would push an unsigned image instead of failing when the `--sign-by` or `--sign-by-sigstore-private-key` options were used.
- Fixed a bug where creating a container with `--userns=auto` that had overlay volume mounts would fail ([#​28758](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28758)).
- Fixed a bug where volume subpaths including a `=` character in the path were handled incorrectly.
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client was unable to add subjects to artifacts with the `podman manifest annotate --subject` and `podman manifest add --artifact subject` commands.
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman manifest add --artifact` command could hang under some circumstances.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman manifest annotate --os-features` command did not properly save the OS features in the manifest.
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman image prune --filter` did not correctly handle filters with values including the `=` character.
- Fixed a bug where Quadlet `.volume` units did not recreate the volume if it was removed in Podman ([#​27862](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27862)).
- Fixed a bug where containers with a failing startup healthcheck would not immediately transition to unhealthy when the startup period ended.
- Fixed a bug where containers started with `--sdnotify=healthy` and a `HealthStartPeriod` longer than the unit's `TimeoutStartSec` could be automatically killed by systemd if the healthcheck took an extended period to become healthy ([#​27290](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27290)).
- Fixed a bug where the `--pids-limit=0` argument to `podman run` and `podman create` was incorrectly setting a process limit, instead of removing the limit, when the `runc` OCI runtime was in use ([#​29826](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29826)).
- Fixed a bug where Quadlet did not search the parent directory of symlinked unit files for drop-in configuration files, which broke using Quadlets defined by root as a rootless user if drop-in overrides were in use ([#​29821](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29821)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman ps` and `podman pod ps` commands would fail when the `--format` argument was used with a format string including `.Label` ([#​29831](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29831)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman cp` command did not respect volume subpaths when copying into a mounted named or image volumes in a container that is not running ([#​29840](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29840) and [#​29857](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29857)).
- Fixed a bug where volume plugins were initialized when they were not required, which could cause early-boot containers started by Quadlet to error on missing plugins that the container was not actually using ([#​28110](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28110)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman export` command, when run by a rootless user on a container created with `--userns=keep-id`, would create an archive with incorrect UIDs and GIDs ([#​29856](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29856)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman system service` command would fail to start when run as a systemd unit and autostarted at the same time as other Podman units ([#​29964](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29964)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman events` command would return incomplete output when using the `file` events backend and `--until` specified with a time in the past ([#​29579](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29579)).
- Fixed a bug where the `podman update` command allowed setting a startup healthcheck on a container without a normal healthcheck.
- Fixed a bug where the remote Podman client's `podman secret rm` command would fail when given an ambiguous name that could match multiple possible secrets.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman machine info` command would report the default VM type and config/image directories, not those used by the current machine.
- Fixed a bug where the `podman inspect` command on containers did not include `CheckpointLog` after a failed container checkpoint ([#​25154](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25154)).

##### API

- The Libpod API now features a new endpoint, `POST /libpod/autoupdate`, which automatically updates containers with the `io.containers.autoupdate` label.
- The Compat API now features a new endpoint, `GET /distribution/{name}/json`, which inspects an image on a registry ([#​17726](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/17726)).
- The Compat Create endpoint for Containers now supports a new field, `HostConfig.Mounts.TmpfsOptions.Options`, to set additional options for tmpfs mounts.
- The Compat Create endpoint for Containers now allows a full Seccomp profile to be passed in the `HostConfig.SecurityOpt` field (instead of a path to a file containing a profile), improving Docker compatibility ([#​27710](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27710)).
- The Compat Push endpoint for Images now supports a new query parameter, `platform`, to push only a single platform-specific manifest instead of the entire list.
- The Compat Info endpoint now includes the status of active OCI runtimes.
- Fixed a bug where the Libpod Create endpoint for Containers required that the `auto` userns mode also specify full UID/GID mappings for the created container.
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Create endpoint for Containers would incorrectly adjust mode when setting tmpfs size.
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Create endpoint for Containers would incorrectly treat a healthcheck of `{}` as the user explicitly requesting no healthcheck, instead of using the image's healthcheck as Docker does ([#​29467](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29467)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Inspect endpoint for Secrets allowed the `showsecret` query parameter, which should be restricted to Libpod API requests only ([#​29570](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29570)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Inspect endpoint for Images included the `Created` field even when it was empty.
- Fixed a bug where the Compat List and Inspect endpoints for Networks did not include `IPRange` in the returned `IPAMConfig` ([#​28378](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28378)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat List endpoint for Containers would error when passed a filter including container statuses supported by Docker but not Podman (`dead` and `restarting`) ([#​28904](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28904)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Stats endpoint for Containers could panic on containers with a memory reservation, but no memory limit, set ([#​29627](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29627)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Stats endpoint for Containers incorrectly populated `system_cpu_usage` and `percpu_stats` when not streaming ([#​28761](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28761), [#​24730](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/24730), [#​25709](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/25709), [#​29912](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29912)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat Info endpoint reported an incorrect cgroup manager when running rootless with the `cgroupfs` cgroup manager ([#​27824](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/27824)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat and Libpod Attach endpoints for Containers would, when doing a logs-only (`stream=0` and `logs=1`) attach, incorrectly reinitialize the container, changing its exit code and status ([#​29664](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29664)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat and Libpod Update endpoints would incorrectly clear a container's restart policy when it was omitted from the request ([#​29790](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29790)).
- Fixed a bug where the Compat and Libpod Start endpoints for Exec sessions would return an error when trying to start an exec session with no standard streams attached without specifying `Detach=true`.
- Fixed a bug where the Libpod Generate Kube endpoint returned the wrong content type ([#​29674](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29674)).
- Numerous fixes to the API's Swagger documentation have been made to ensure it accurately documents the REST API.

##### Misc

- Fixed a number of low-level resource leaks in various parts of Podman.
- Waiting for `gvproxy` to start when starting a `podman machine` VM now uses a notification socket, instead of polling, improving reliability and startup time.
- Updated documentation for the `--image-volume` option to `podman create` and `podman run` to remove the deprecated `bind` option and add the new default, `anonymous`, which was not shown as a valid option. Using the deprecated `bind` option now prints a warning.
- Updated Buildah to v1.46.0
- Updated Common to v0.70.0
- Updated Image to v5.42.1
- Updated Storage to v1.64.2

</details>

Publish Release run 41557 (v0.11.9, PR #376) failed with "This PR head did not pass Prepare Release" although 402a470 carried a success `Release / Qualified candidate` status from run 858.

Cause: `publish-release.yml` matches the status `target_url` against `$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs/`. Prepare Release ran on a pool runner registered with `http://forgejo.forgejo.svc.cluster.local`, so the status URL uses that host; the first Publish attempt landed on a runner whose server URL is `https://forgejo.bryantserver.com` (its checkout fetched from there), so the prefix did not match. A rerun on a pool runner passed and tagged v0.11.9.

Fix: match on the repository path and run number, independent of the host the runner was registered with (or check the status creator instead of the URL). Same check exists in `release.yml` for an existing release PR; review both. Also find which runner registered with the public URL.

title: Publish Release refuses a qualified PR when it runs on a runner with a different server URL

body:
Closes #377.

Publish Release found the Prepare Release run by requiring the qualification status URL to start with its own runner's `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`. Cluster pool runners use `http://forgejo.forgejo.svc.cluster.local`, while the annex CI runner registers with the cluster at `https://forgejo.bryantserver.com` (bryantserver/annex `nix/services/ci-runner.nix:88`; it is runner `62383437-…`, which took run 41557's first attempt). So a qualified PR was refused whenever Publish landed on the other kind of runner.

`.forgejo/scripts/qualified-run.py` now reads the run number from a URL whose path is exactly `/<repo>/actions/runs/<n>`, on any http(s) host. It keeps every earlier condition: the exact context, the success state, a complete status list, a digits-only run number, the same error message, and exactly one run.

The host was never a source of trust. Anyone who can post a status can write any URL. Trust comes from the next steps, which are unchanged: they look up that run number in this repository's API (`release.yml`, success, dispatched on main for the same channel) and require `Qualified release commit: <candidate>` in its job log.

Tests (`tests/test_release_promotion.py`):
- The helper accepts both runner hosts and refuses other repositories, `/jobs` suffixes, queries, fragments, credentials, non-http URLs, bad run numbers, non-success states, the wrong context, a missing URL, no run, two runs and a truncated list.
- The real Publish verify step runs against a stubbed API, with `GITHUB_SERVER_URL` set to the public URL and the status written with the cluster URL. It fails on main with "This PR head did not pass Prepare Release". With matching hosts the old step passes (the control run), so the failure comes from the defect. It passes with this change.
- Against the live v0.11.9 candidate (402a470), the helper prints 858.

Checks: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_release_promotion.py`, actionlint and ruff (E9,F) are clean. Codex reviewed it and found no trust regression; its one finding, the missing workflow-level test, is the step test above.
